comparisons.success_condition: Required face coverage and limited post-breading grips, rather than repeatable bounded carriage stops.
comparisons.reason: Deformable coating and handling economy test a wholly different ability.

comparisons.objective: Break a jar-lid seal with a lifter, then twist off and set down the lid, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a lever under a lid edge, pry, stabilize the jar, and unscrew; no hex-socket locking or response-driven collar tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Seal broken, lid unlatched and placed flat, jar stable, hands clear, and no spill-related tilt violation.
comparisons.reason: Tool-assisted opening shares rotation and stabilization only at a generic level.

comparisons.objective: Fill a narrow-necked bottle with beads, versus adjust and test a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Transfer and guide many small loose objects through a narrow opening; no fastener, collar, or dynamic-test interaction.
comparisons.success_condition: A specified fraction of beads settles inside the bottle.
comparisons.reason: Granular transfer is unrelated to mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Interrupt cube sorting to close a filling-tank inlet after an alarm, versus commission a damper under lockout.
comparisons.physical_skill: Monitor a timed process, actuate a valve at the correct interval, and resume sorting; no fine tool engagement or iterative parameter tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Cubes sorted and inlet closed after alarm but before overflow, with early closure penalized.
comparisons.reason: Timed alarm response and concurrent sorting differ from measured damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Extract a case leaning on a locker door and place it upright without tipping or dropping, versus tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually support a load while opening an obstructed door and transporting it upright.
comparisons.success_condition: Case never exceeds tip/drop limits and stands released on the mat.
comparisons.reason: Load support during access and transport tests a different physical skill and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Grease a pivot through a nipple without leakage, versus commission a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely seat and hold a grease coupler while the other hand cycles a pump, then remove and stow it; candidate instead adjusts and locks a fine rotary control.
comparisons.success_condition: Four valid pump shots with a sealed coupler, no leak, and tool stowed; no stopping-response measurements.
comparisons.reason: Both demand alignment and bimanual force control, but fluid delivery through a maintained seal is a different tested ability.

comparisons.objective: Route a connected cable between posts and secure its final clip while preserving an existing fixing, versus tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually manipulate an articulated wire, route it around obstacles, and seat it in a spring clip.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct route, both clips retained, required hand participation, release, clearance, and low wire speed; separation or upstream release fails.
comparisons.reason: Cable routing and compliant-object retention are meaningfully different from precision rotary adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Fit and hand-tighten an oxygen regulator on a pin-index cylinder valve, versus tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a yoke, engage two indexing pins and a washer face, then tighten a T-handle screw while controlling a bulky regulator.
comparisons.success_condition: Regulator seated within alignment tolerances, tightened to at least 0.75 N·m, stable and released without drop/tip hazards.
comparisons.reason: This is keyed assembly and fastening; it does not adjust a parameter based on repeated dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Remove capped needles from Luer-lock syringes safely, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize each syringe while unscrewing a small capped needle without axial cap separation, then optionally place it in a sharps tray.
comparisons.success_condition: Needles unscrewed and removed while caps never expose a needle; syringe displacement is limited.
comparisons.reason: Small-thread manipulation is shared only generically; the safety mechanism and endpoint differ.

comparisons.objective: Open a sealed cocktail shaker with a correctly placed bounded strike, versus tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize nested tins, deliver an impact at the wide-gap side, separate them, and prevent spilling.
comparisons.success_condition: Seal broken specifically by a 0.15–1.0 m/s qualified blow, tins upright and released, with no dent, spill, or fall.
comparisons.reason: Impact placement and seal release are different from adjustment followed by measured impact absorption.

comparisons.objective: Measure subfloor flatness and report PASS/FAIL, versus tune a damper to repeatable stopping behavior.
comparisons.physical_skill: Set a straightedge, insert/read a wedge at the deepest gap, and place a classification puck; no fastener or iterative adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Wedge reading matches the deepest trough within 0.3 mm and the correct threshold label is selected.
comparisons.reason: Both use physical measurements to guide an action, but metrology/classification is not closed-loop mechanism commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Compare two sleds' friction using gravity-ramp stopping distances, versus adjust a damper until carriage stops meet safety limits.
comparisons.physical_skill: Release sleds under controlled conditions, observe stopping distances, compare materials, and select the higher-friction sled; no mechanical setting change or relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Both valid stopping measurements differ by over 30 mm and only the higher-friction sled is placed on the mat.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared dynamic-measurement primitive, but it tests comparative identification, whereas the candidate tests fine adjustment, locking, and iterative control of one energy absorber under force/travel/rebound constraints.

comparisons.objective: Choose fitting tweezers and peel protective film from a display carrier, versus commission a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select a tool by slot fit, stabilize a loose carrier, grip a film tab, and perform controlled adhesive peeling.
comparisons.success_condition: All adhesive detached without excessive carrier motion or premature seam separation; film and tools stowed and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Tool selection and adhesive peeling are materially different from socket/collar adjustment and dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Receive a terminal block from a person and latch it onto a loose DIN rail; unlike commissioning a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gentle handover, rail alignment, snap-fit insertion, and optional rail stabilization versus hex-bit use, collar adjustment, and dynamic-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a clean force-limited handover and a precisely seated rail latch without moving the rail; no damping-cycle or setting-retention test. Rubric is numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: The record tests human-safe transfer followed by snap-fit assembly, a meaningfully different ability from unlocking, tuning, relocking, and dynamically validating a damper.

comparisons.objective: Pull a stiff sliding window open through a fragile handle; not adjust or commission the damper causing resistance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Regulated pulling through a D-handle while limiting load versus fine hex-tool seating, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and iterative tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores handle-mediated sash travel and fails on handle or window damage; it does not alter a setting or evaluate repeatable stopping behavior. Rubric is numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: Although its fixture may use a viscous damper, the tested action is force-limited window opening, not damper adjustment and lock verification.

comparisons.objective: Measure two leveled scoops of formula into a bottle; unrelated to shock-absorber commissioning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scoop dipping, strike-off leveling, controlled pouring, and spill avoidance versus fine tool use and mechanical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the correct powder mass, bar-leveling history, limited spill, and released scoop; no mechanical setting or dynamic stop test. Rubric is numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: It tests bulk-material measurement and pouring rather than adjustment, locking, or energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Rinse a glass by depressing a spring valve and leave it draining; not tune a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Centre and sustain a press through a grasped glass, then relocate it, versus manipulating a tiny screw and collar and interpreting carriage response.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires 1.5 seconds of covered valve actuation and stable rim-down placement, with zero for uncovered spray; no adjustable setting or repeat-cycle criterion. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: A sprung press-and-hold operation does not test the candidate's fine adjustment, relocking, or iterative dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Make a slicer safe by closing its gauge plate, release its carriage, and place the carriage for cleaning.
comparisons.physical_skill: Turn large knobs through multiple rotations, obey an interlock, and carry a 1.6 kg carriage versus small-socket tool engagement and fine collar tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires gauge closure before motion, release-knob travel, safe blade-zone avoidance, and flat carriage placement; no damping-response optimization. Numeric rubric is complete across versions.
comparisons.reason: Both involve knobs and safety sequencing, but the slicer tests interlocked disassembly and carrying, not commissioning an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Mesh and seat a loose rack in a parallel gripper so both jaws move symmetrically.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tooth-phase alignment, rack insertion, meshing, and functional jaw travel versus loosening a lock, rotating a collar, and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires seated racks, jaw-centre error within about 3 mm, at least 15 mm travel, release, and stillness; no force-response or stopping-cycle test. Rubric is numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: Precision gear-phase assembly and symmetric motion are materially different tested abilities from damper adjustment and verification.

comparisons.objective: Move four visually identical cups with hidden masses without crushing or dropping them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Infer payload through lifting and adapt grip force per cup versus adjust a mechanical damping control using impact response.
comparisons.success_condition: Each cup must be side-gripped, unbuckled, unslipped, upright, released, and on the tray; no tool, lock, or damper setting. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Shared adaptation from physical feedback is generic; the record tests compliant grip-force selection, not setting and retaining an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Open the clean-ice bin and deliver uncontaminated ice with a scoop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lid removal, scoop manipulation, source selection, pouring, and contamination avoidance versus fine adjustment and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires clean-source scoop delivery with persistent hygiene history and settled release; no mechanical tuning criterion. Rubric is detailed and numeric.
comparisons.reason: This is hygiene-aware bulk-object handling, not a damper commissioning task.

comparisons.objective: Put clean ice into a bowl with the scoop while avoiding fish-source contamination.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove a lid, scoop loose cubes, transport them, and pour cleanly versus hex-bit/collar manipulation and guarded dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Full credit requires a clean delivered cube, lid-opening history, no contamination, and released settling; no adjustment or lock retention. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: The task tests source discrimination and hygienic tool use, materially separate from tuning a shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Pack three cases into two locker bays while ensuring nothing rests on the fragile blue case.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plan stacking order and place rigid cases flat in tight bays versus fine tool use and iterative mechanical adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires all cases stowed with at most two per bay and no grey case loading the blue one; no dynamic-response test. Rubric is numeric, though simulated glass breakage is only a scored rule.
comparisons.reason: It tests constrained packing and load-path reasoning rather than damper setting, locking, and verification.

comparisons.objective: Re-sort six bottles between crowded shelf levels while preserving every neighboring bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Horizontal constrained extraction, staging, replacement, and multi-object collision avoidance versus small-tool engagement and tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires all bottles on color-matched shelves, stable for two seconds, with irreversible fall/tilt/workspace failures; no damping criterion. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Crowded multi-object sorting is a different tested manipulation family from commissioning an adjustable shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Perform a prove-test-prove voltage-detector procedure and stop safely when the proof source fails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate buttons, manipulate a long hot stick, touch specified targets, and condition action on indicator state versus fine collar and setscrew manipulation.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires ordered self-test, proof, bar test, and re-proof, or a timed safe retreat on failed proof; no dynamic mechanical tuning. Rubric is complete for both seeds.
comparisons.reason: Both require safety sequencing and physical verification, but the record tests electrical-procedure compliance with a long tool, not damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Uncork a wine bottle while keeping it in its cradle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the bottle, screw a worm into cork, operate extraction leverage, and remove the cork versus adjust and lock a damping collar.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires cork extraction and separation without displacing the bottle; no carriage stopping or setting-retention measurement. Rubric is complete, despite substantial mechanism changes across versions.
comparisons.reason: Shared turning and bimanual stabilization are generic; cork engagement and high-force extraction are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Selectively detach ripe tomatoes at their knuckles and place them in a tray without harming fruit or truss.
comparisons.physical_skill: Gentle fruit grasping and bending at an abscission joint versus hex-tool insertion, collar rotation, and mechanical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both red tomatoes detached by bending and deposited, green fruit retained, and no crush, pull-tear, or drop. Numeric rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Selective compliant harvesting tests delicate bending and damage avoidance, not adjustable energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Bend a copper tube to 90 degrees while compensating for hidden springback.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a free lever bender, make irreversible bends, relax to observe springback, and correct incrementally versus manipulating and locking a damper control.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a released 87–93 degree tube with the lever relaxed and bender intact; no repeated impact-stop validation. Rubric is numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: Both use iterative physical feedback, but the tube task tests irreversible forming and springback compensation rather than reversible damper setting and energy dissipation.

comparisons.objective: Fit and lock a suction tool onto a robot quick-change flange.
comparisons.physical_skill: Carry and align a tool plate, hold it against a flange, and actuate a locking ring bimanually versus fine hex/collar adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the correct tool locked and hanging after release, with arms withdrawn; it does not test a tuned dynamic response. Numeric seating and lock thresholds are supplied.
comparisons.reason: This is aligned tool mounting and latching, a different ability from commissioning a shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Remove a worn toothbrush head and install a new one, with some versions also opening its clamshell pack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, axial press-fit extraction/insertion, disposal, and optional package opening versus socket engagement and collar tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the new head fully seated, worn head binned, and arms returned; no impact testing or setting retention. Rubric is complete across versions.
comparisons.reason: Axial press-fit replacement is materially different from adjusting and validating a damper.

comparisons.objective: Remove a named cartridge fuse with an insulated puller by rocking it out one end at a time.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick up tong puller, grip the correct fuse, lever sequentially against clips, and transport it without disturbing neighbors versus rotate and lock a setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires F2 removed while held by the tool and placed in a tray, with irreversible failure if F1/F3 move; no damping-cycle criterion. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: The record tests target selection and asymmetric lever extraction, not shock-absorber commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Unlock a twist-lock extension pole, set its length to a mark, relock it, and verify it under axial load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply a bimanual counter-torque to coaxial tubes, slide to length, reverse the twist, clear hands, and load-test; candidate instead uses a tiny hex socket and fine collar with iterative impact-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires 84–86 cm length, lock angle near the initial state, and under 2 mm shortening under 50 N for two seconds; candidate requires two acceptable dynamic stops under energy, travel, rebound, force, and drift bounds. Rubrics are numeric and complete.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest workflow-level analogue—unlock, adjust, relock, verify—but it tests counter-rotation, telescoping length, and static friction-lock capacity rather than tool-mediated damping adjustment and dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Place a shackle around a towing lug, insert its pin through three aligned holes, and screw it fully home.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual part alignment, close-clearance pin insertion, thread engagement, and repeated rotational regrasps versus loosen/reseat a hex bit and rotate an adjustment collar.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the pin through both ears and lug with its collar within 1 mm of the ear; no response tuning or dynamic stop test. Final screw-pin version has a complete numeric rubric.
comparisons.reason: Threaded pin assembly through aligned holes is a meaningfully different tested ability, despite shared tool-free rotation and locking.

comparisons.objective: Press a copper tube into two self-closing clamps until both reach their second locking click.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a long tube simultaneously with two clamp mouths and apply insertion force through two detents versus fine rotary adjustment and tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires both clamps locked, tube seated straight, hands clear, and one-second stillness; no iterative damping measurement. Rubric is complete, while click forces are disclosed approximations.
comparisons.reason: This tests long-part alignment and snap-fit insertion, not commissioning an adjustable energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Load an IV set by seating the upper fitment first and then pressing the safety clamp home without twisting or stretching tubing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate keyed rigid fitments connected by a soft segment, preserve seating, and press past sprung pins versus rigid fine-tool and collar operations.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires ordered seating, bounded lift and stretch, untwisted tubing, clearance, and a two-second hold; no dynamic-response tuning. Rubric is detailed and numeric.
comparisons.reason: It tests deformable-line management between keyed seats, materially different from the rigid damper task.

comparisons.objective: Uniformly heat-shrink a sleeve over a cable lug and safely stow the heat gun.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate cable rotation with noncontact heat-tool traversal and exposure control versus contact-based hex/collar manipulation and impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires all sleeve stations recovered, both ends sealed, no charring or contact, gun off and stowed, and hands clear; no damper setting. Rubric is complete though thermal behavior is a coded approximation.
comparisons.reason: Controlled distributed heating is a separate ability from mechanical adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Find a sealed tube's hidden balance point and hang it level from one conveyor hook.
comparisons.physical_skill: Perform diagnostic test lifts, observe tilt, regrasp at a new point, and place a long load on a narrow cradle versus adjust a small mechanism and run carriage tests.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires released, still hanging within 3 degrees for two seconds, with permanent failure on drop or return to the table; no lock or damping-response thresholds. Rubric is complete.
comparisons.reason: Shared iterative physical inference is generic; hidden-centre-of-mass regrasping and single-point hanging are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Clear a rigid obstruction and insert a knife into the center slot of a holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove and place an obstructing toy, then align and deeply insert a long thin blade versus fine hex-tool use, collar adjustment, and response testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires safe released toy removal and knife insertion within tight pose, depth, speed, and clearance limits for one second; no tuning criterion. Rubric is detailed and complete.
comparisons.reason: Prerequisite obstacle removal followed by precision insertion does not overlap the candidate's tested commissioning ability.

comparisons.objective: Transport an opaque collar along a curved protected guide while maintaining clearance under changing occlusion; candidate commissions and dynamically tests an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Guide-threaded transport and view-dependent collision avoidance versus recessed hex engagement, captive-screw loosening, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded test actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Collar must remain threaded, avoid prohibited contact, reach its support, be released, and remain still; exact numeric rubric is not included in the available record body. Candidate instead requires two force-, travel-, rebound-, drift-, and hard-stop-safe impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is occluded constrained transport, not adjustment locking followed by measured dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Safely mix two open test tubes by side-to-side waggling; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual grasping, lifting, rhythmic lateral agitation, and rack replacement versus fine hex-tool use, collar adjustment, reacquisition, and iterative response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Each tube needs 12 valid lateral swings, both returned and released; vertical shaking or tilt over 60 degrees fails. Candidate instead evaluates axial energy absorption, force/travel limits, rebound, and setting retention over two cycles.
comparisons.reason: Safe open-vessel agitation and damper commissioning test different manipulation and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Apply PTFE tape correctly to a pipe thread; candidate adjusts, locks, and validates a hydraulic damper setting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled dispenser orbiting, tape payout, tearing, and tail pressing versus inserting a fine hex bit, loosening a captive lock, rotating a collar, and reacquiring its moved socket.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires 3–6 clockwise wraps with specified coverage, bare first thread, pressed tail, and released dispenser. Candidate requires two repeatable safe dynamic stops without bottoming, overload, rebound, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Although both include rotation and tool clearance, tape winding mechanics and the scored sealed-thread preparation outcome are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Tighten and align a hook using a toggle bolt behind a hollow panel; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain outward reaction load while ratcheting a Phillips screw and controlling plate alignment versus captive setscrew access, bit withdrawal, fine collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Hook must be flush, within 3 degrees, released, and pass the later 5 N pull-test version; losing the toggle fails. Candidate must meet energy, velocity, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits for two impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both use a recessed tool and locking rotation, but the toggle task tests reaction-torque fastening of a fixture, not iterative dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Reconnect a sink pop-up stopper to its pivot rod; candidate commissions an adjustable damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Blindly align and capture a stopper eye with a lateral pivot rod and reassemble drain linkage versus hex engagement, collar adjustment, relocking, and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: The drain linkage must reconnect and operate the stopper; candidate instead requires quantified safe and repeatable carriage stopping. The record provides no comparable damper-response thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Hidden linkage capture and functional drain operation are meaningfully different from tuning and validating energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Mount a filled malt cup around a fixed mixer spindle so its rim seats in the guide and activates the motor; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tilt-and-lift insertion around a spindle, precise seating on a stepped rest, and spill avoidance versus fine tool insertion, lock manipulation, collar rotation, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup must seat on the run step, lift the switch pin, contain the spindle, remain upright, released, and still; excessive tilt or falling fails. Candidate uses axial impact, force, rebound, and setting-drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: Constrained vessel mounting and switch engagement do not test adjustment locking or response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Attach a price ticket through a garment care label without piercing the shirt; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift and hold a thin flap while aiming a needle, squeezing a trigger, and withdrawing it versus hex-bit seating, captive-lock manipulation, collar tuning, and test control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Fire once through a label held at least 2 cm clear, never pierce the shirt, withdraw the needle, and release the label. Candidate requires two safe dynamic-stop cycles within force and travel limits.
comparisons.reason: Protected thin-flap piercing is unrelated in mechanism and outcome to damper adjustment and dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Remove a glovebox, replace a cabin air filter, and reinstall the glovebox; candidate tunes and validates a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Release stops/hinges, extract and orient a filter, insert it into a housing, and restore the glovebox versus fine hex access, collar rotation, relocking, and iterative response measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct filter replacement and complete glovebox restoration are required; candidate instead scores bounded energy absorption and repeatable stopping without overload or drift.
comparisons.reason: Module access and replacement do not exercise setting adjustment or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Push a peg fully home despite a hidden obstruction without forcing it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compliant probing, obstruction diagnosis, realignment, and controlled insertion versus fine tool engagement, lock/collar sequencing, and iterative impact-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Peg must be fully seated without prohibited forcing or damage; available record details do not specify candidate-like cycle metrics. Candidate requires two quantified safe axial stops.
comparisons.reason: Shared force sensitivity is generic; hidden-obstruction insertion is a different tested ability from adjustment locking and dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Operate meter test switches in a safety-critical order and insert a test plug; candidate adjusts and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential handle actuation and keyed plug insertion with interlock awareness versus recessed hex manipulation, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and physical impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified switches must end in exact states, the plug must be inserted, and the red switch must never open while orange is closed. Candidate instead enforces lockout, tool clearance, force/travel limits, and repeatable stopping.
comparisons.reason: Electrical switching order and plug insertion test procedural interlocking, not mechanical-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Carry a full cup past an open laptop to a coaster without spilling; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stable transport of an open liquid container around a protected obstacle versus small-tool access, collar adjustment, relocking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup must reach the coaster without spill or laptop contact; candidate requires two impact cycles satisfying energy, force, travel, rebound, and drift bounds.
comparisons.reason: Protected liquid transport is materially unrelated to adjustment and dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Install an oversized U-joint cross through a yoke using a staged push, swing, and recenter sequence; candidate tunes a damper.

comparisons.success_condition: Both journals must be equally seated in their ear holes after the cross is leveled; candidate instead requires a retained setting and two safe dynamic stops.
comparisons.reason: The U-joint task tests geometric assembly through a narrow gap, not response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Open an anti-static bag, remove one battery, and place it upright in a holder; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Zipper-slider manipulation, bag access, selective extraction, and holder insertion versus fine hex access, collar tuning, socket reacquisition, and test actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one cell must be removed and correctly oriented in the holder while the other remains bagged, with arms returned. Candidate uses dynamic force, travel, rebound, and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: Packaging access and selective component placement test different mechanics and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a compression pipe joint with the olive and nut in order and tighten it a turn past snug; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequence loose fitting parts, insert pipe home, establish thread engagement, detect snug, and turn with a spanner versus loosen a captive setscrew, withdraw a hex bit, tune a collar, reacquire the socket, and cycle a fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct part order, full pipe insertion, and specified post-snug tightening define success; candidate requires repeatable bounded dynamic absorption and no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both involve tightening, but compression-joint assembly tests part sequencing and leak-joint preload rather than adjustable damping behavior.

comparisons.objective: Clear a jammed printer card with both hands and resume printing; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinated bimanual traction on a resisting sheet/card while avoiding tearing and restoring printer operation versus small-tool access, collar rotation, and iterative impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Jam must be removed intact and printing resumed; candidate instead requires two safe, repeatable carriage stops under numeric physical limits.
comparisons.reason: Jammed-media extraction and restoration test a different physical ability and end state.

comparisons.objective: Restock a twin-roll tissue dispenser by moving the stub to reserve, installing a new primary roll, and locking the cover; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Roll removal/insertion, spindle allocation, cover closure, and key/lock handling versus fine hex engagement, captive setscrew manipulation, collar tuning, and guarded dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Old roll must occupy reserve, new roll primary, cover closed and locked. Candidate instead evaluates stopping travel, forces, rebound, and retained adjustment over two cycles.
comparisons.reason: The shared generic notion of locking does not make consumable restocking equivalent to dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Lower a loaded hotel pan level into a steam-table well and release it; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load balancing, close-clearance lowering, flange seating, and spill avoidance versus fine tool insertion, collar rotation, relocking, and iterative test control.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan flange must rest correctly on the well, level and released, without loss/spill; candidate requires repeatable bounded axial stops.
comparisons.reason: Heavy level placement into a recess tests load coordination, not tuning and locking a response element.

comparisons.objective: Cut a taped carton seam without damaging a product 6 mm below, then retract the blade; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Depth-controlled cutting along a seam and safe blade retraction versus recessed hex manipulation, fine collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete the 40 cm seam cut without reaching the product and leave the blade retracted; candidate uses force, energy, travel, rebound, and drift measurements.
comparisons.reason: Controlled cutting near protected contents is a different manipulation and safety outcome.

comparisons.objective: Push a shower cartridge through O-ring resistance and retain it with a U-clip; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply sustained axial seating force while aligning and sliding a transverse retaining clip past ears versus loosen-adjust-relock with a fine hex tool and evaluate dynamic response.
comparisons.success_condition: Cartridge must remain flush and mechanically retained after release; candidate requires two impact cycles without bottoming, overload, excessive rebound, or collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Both concern retention, but sustained insertion plus clip capture is materially different from adjustable damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Pipe a joined decorative shell border on a cake; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Continuous bag-pressure control coordinated with nozzle motion and release to form repeated shells versus hex-tool insertion, collar adjustment, relocking, and physical testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Distinct joined shells with ridges and tapered tails must span the marks without fouling the board; candidate requires quantified repeatable stopping behavior.
comparisons.reason: Extrusion shaping and food-surface cleanliness share no meaningful tested mechanism with damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Transfer all crackers while excluding a desiccant packet; candidate commissions an adjustable damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual/tactile item discrimination and repeated selective transfer versus precision hex access, lock/collar sequencing, and iterative response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: All crackers must reach the basket while the desiccant remains excluded; the available record lacks detailed numeric rubric thresholds. Candidate instead requires two safe dynamic-stop cycles.
comparisons.reason: Selective sorting is clearly unrelated; missing numeric thresholds do not create plausible duplication.

comparisons.objective: Move a lamp closer before placing its attached plug in a tray without pulling the cord dangerously; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manage a tethered object and articulated cord, reposition the lamp, and place the plug versus fine hex engagement, collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Lamp must remain upright and undamaged, plug end in the tray, cord not over-tensioned or detached, and hands released. Candidate instead requires retained adjustment and bounded repeated impacts.
comparisons.reason: Tether management and safe plug delivery test different mechanics from shock-absorber commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Align, push, and quarter-turn a bayonet cap until mechanically locked; candidate adjusts and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed lug-slot alignment, axial spring compression, and rotation under contact to a stop versus recessed hex insertion, captive screw loosening, separate collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap must be centered, upright, rotated over 80 degrees, retained under the roof, released, and still. Candidate requires a locked setting plus two force-, travel-, rebound-, and drift-safe impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest lock-by-rotation primitive, but it tests mating and latching a separate cap, not changing a setting, relocking its moved socket, or validating dynamic performance.

comparisons.objective: Install three gears on shafts while finding tooth phase and meshing adjacent pairs; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bore-shaft insertion, contact-guided tooth phasing, sequential meshing, and release versus fine hex access, collar tuning, socket reacquisition, and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: All gears must be seated within 2 mm/1 mm/3 degrees, meshed, still, released, and clear for 1 second in the final versions. Candidate instead scores dynamic stopping and setting retention.
comparisons.reason: Gear-train assembly and tooth-phase discovery are materially different from adjustable damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a glued panel with alternating clamp faces and bounded pressure; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Position a spare bar clamp, close multiple sliding jaws, balance panel alignment, and regulate clamping force versus fine hex insertion, collar rotation, relocking, and iterative response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Joint must close and stay level with three alternating snug clamps at 1–6 N; over 6 N for 0.5 seconds fails. Candidate instead requires two axial impacts within energy, velocity, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Both require bounded force and locking a setting, but panel clamping tests distributed static fixturing, whereas the candidate tests dynamic energy absorption and iterative commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Undo a tight bolt with a ratchet after correcting the ratchet direction; candidate commissions and locks a hydraulic damper through iterative impact tests.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR uses lever flipping, socket seating, and repeated ratchet strokes. Candidate uses a 1.5 mm hex bit, captive setscrew, fine collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires at least one turn of bolt removal, tool return, and no damaging tightening. Candidate requires two safe, repeatable ≥0.85 J stops within travel, velocity, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Tool rotation is shared, but the tested abilities and outcome are materially different: fastener removal/tool-mode reasoning versus locked dynamic damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Compress and lock spring tongs, then place them in a cutlery tray; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber for controlled dynamic stopping.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires squeezing sprung arms, pulling a lock tab, and placing the locked utensil. Candidate requires fine tool insertion, captive-screw manipulation, collar adjustment, reacquisition, and guarded testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR succeeds when released tongs remain locked in the tray for 2 s. Candidate succeeds after two consecutive compliant impact cycles with no bottoming, overload, rebound, tool loss, damage, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both include locking, but the mechanisms, manipulation sequence, and tested physical outcome are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Tilt a cabinet shelf through a narrow opening and lower it onto four pins; candidate commissions a hydraulic axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests bimanual large-object roll, constrained insertion, leveling, and four-point placement. Candidate tests fine hex access, collar rotation, moving-socket reacquisition, locking, and iterative physical tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires four-pin support, ≤1° level/square alignment, back placement, release, and a 1 s hold. Candidate requires repeated force-, travel-, rebound-, energy-, and drift-bounded carriage stops.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, mechanism, or success-outcome overlap beyond generic alignment.

comparisons.objective: Install two hook-in gondola brackets and seat a shelf; candidate adjusts and validates a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires pitched hook insertion, swing-down seating, repeated bracket placement, and bimanual shelf handling. Candidate requires fine tool engagement, captive setscrew loosening/relocking, collar adjustment, and dynamic feedback iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: PR scores seated hooks/tongues and a stable released shelf, with drop and sequencing failures. Candidate scores two repeatable safe impact stops and rejects bottoming, excessive forces, rebound, drift, damage, and unsafe cycling.
comparisons.reason: Hook-and-shelf assembly tests constrained installation, not adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Spread a sprung delta-printer arm pair and fit its sockets over effector ball studs; candidate tunes a hydraulic damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires holding two arms apart against spring force while aligning two sockets and moving an effector into them. Candidate requires small-tool insertion, screw/collar manipulation, socket reacquisition, and impact-response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both ball sockets seated, effector flat, hands clear, and 1 s stability. Candidate requires two bounded-energy carriage stops without travel, force, rebound, or retention faults.
comparisons.reason: Spring-loaded dual-socket assembly and hydraulic commissioning test different physical abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Configure a control panel from a setup sheet and initiate a two-hand start; candidate physically adjusts a damper, then operates a guarded test control and tunes from measured response.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR manipulates switches, a detented dial, sliders, and two buttons based on printed settings. Candidate seats a fine hex tool, manipulates a captive lock and small collar, reacquires a moved socket, and iterates using real carriage dynamics.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires exact P2 control settings and a synchronized 2 s two-button start, with forbidden-button failures. Candidate requires two consecutive impact cycles satisfying energy, travel, velocity, force, rebound, and drift constraints.
comparisons.reason: Guarded control actuation and a rotary setting are shared primitives, but PR tests instruction-following panel setup; the candidate tests mechanical locking plus closed-loop dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Free an entangled tote strap and lower the tote safely; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires deformable-entanglement handling, hazard recognition, tote support, and careful lowering. Candidate requires precision tool access, screw/collar manipulation, and iterative rigid-body impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the tote released on the table, rake retained, and contents preserved. Candidate requires two safe, repeatable axial stops within numeric energy, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: The deformable hazard-removal task has no meaningful overlap with damper adjustment or dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Load and orient four blanks into a close-clearance gravity magazine; candidate adjusts and tests a hydraulic damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests repeated grasping, yaw alignment, release into a narrow channel, and stacking. Candidate tests fine hex insertion, captive locking, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and response-driven adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR scores the number of flat, supported, stationary blanks fully inside the magazine. Candidate requires two consecutive compliant carriage stops with no hard-stop strike, overload, rebound, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Close-clearance insertion and stacking do not test mechanical adjustment, retention, or dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Fasten a screw and coupling nut through opposite sides of a plate; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires bimanual coaxial alignment, screw insertion, nut stabilization, and multiple thread turns. Candidate requires fine hex access to a captive screw, independent collar rotation, moved-socket reacquisition, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the screw through the plate, caught, turned at least 1.5 turns, snug, released, and stable. Candidate requires a retained setting and two bounded dynamic stops without damage or safety violations.
comparisons.reason: Both involve threaded rotation, but PR tests creating a bolted joint; the candidate uses a captive lock as one step in tuning a dynamic mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a cake pan and plate together, invert them, and remove the pan; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires coordinated bimanual clamping, lifting, 180° inversion, placement, and separation. Candidate requires fine tool insertion, collar manipulation, locking, and iterative physical-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the inverted cake centered on a plate on the stand, pan removed, and 2 s stability. Candidate requires two repeatable safe stops under explicit energy, travel, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: The large-object bimanual inversion task is unrelated to precision adjustment and impact commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Orient stack-nest totes correctly and stack them without contacting contained parts; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests reading mating geometry, 180° reorientation, large-object alignment, and controlled lowering. Candidate tests small-tool engagement, captive lock manipulation, collar setting, and dynamic feedback iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both grey totes released on ledges, parts unmoved, and no prior nesting below the ledges. Candidate requires two safe impact cycles and rejects bottoming, overload, rebound, damage, and drift.
comparisons.reason: Geometry-based tote orientation and stacking do not test adjustable damping or tool-mediated locking.

comparisons.objective: Insert a stripped cable into a lug, actuate a crimping press, and return the finished cable; candidate commissions a hydraulic damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires bimanual cable alignment and depth control while pressing a lever. Candidate requires recessed hex insertion, captive-screw torque, fine collar rotation, moved-socket reacquisition, and repeated test adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires a depth- and angle-correct crimp, lever release, cable extraction/return, and arm clearance; its simulated hold is event-based and not pull-tested. Candidate requires physically retained adjustment and two force-, travel-, energy-, rebound-, and drift-compliant cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both include guarded machine actuation, but cable insertion/crimping and dynamic damper tuning are materially different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Insert a cotter pin through a clevis and plastically bend both legs to retain it; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires small-part insertion and irreversible opposed-leg bending. Candidate requires reversible hex-tool engagement, captive-screw loosening, collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires seating, both legs bent ≥45°, release, stability, and no excessive rebending. Candidate requires two repeatable impact stops and no bottoming, overload, rebound, damage, or collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Although both secure mechanisms, irreversible cotter deformation is not the candidate's adjustable locking-and-testing ability.

comparisons.objective: Select and stack lighting gels to reproduce a reference color; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests visual color-combination reasoning and planar stacking. Candidate tests fine mechanical tool use, collar adjustment, locking, and iterative evaluation of physical impact response.
comparisons.success_condition: PR succeeds when the transmitted computed color matches the reference with the correct stable stack and untouched reference. Candidate succeeds through two physically safe, repeatable stops within mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: The PR's core ability is subtractive-color selection, with no meaningful mechanical or outcome overlap.

comparisons.objective: File a steel block flat to a scribed line without overcutting; candidate tunes a hydraulic damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires bimanual file control, balanced pressure, directional strokes, and material-removal regulation. Candidate requires fine hex access, collar rotation, locking, and iterative impact-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires specified remaining height/flatness, no cut below the line, tool return, and a stable hold. Candidate requires two energy-, force-, travel-, rebound-, and drift-bounded stop cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve feedback and force-sensitive adjustment, but material removal to geometry and dynamic damper commissioning are meaningfully different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Torque a busbar lug bolt to a click-wrench signal without overshoot; candidate sets and locks a damper, then validates stopping behavior.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests steady wrench pulling and rapid cessation at a one-shot mechanical click. Candidate tests recessed bit insertion, captive screw loosening/tightening, fine collar rotation, moved-socket reacquisition, and iterative test cycles.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires a click and peak torque within 90–110%, with no reversal or overtorque and hands clear. Candidate requires two consecutive safe stops plus force, travel, velocity, rebound, and ≤2° drift compliance.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize excessive force and use a tool, but PR is single-event torque control; the candidate's core outcome is tuning and retaining dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Remove a cap and connect an M12 cable while holding a loose sensor against coupling-ring drag; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires cap handling, connector alignment, thread engagement, bimanual counter-holding, and coupling-ring rotation. Candidate requires fine hex insertion, captive-screw loosening, collar rotation, socket reacquisition after motion, relocking, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the cap in a tray, connector tight, sensor stable, hands released, and arms returned. Candidate requires retained adjustment and two safe dynamic stop cycles within energy, travel, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Rotary locking and stabilization are shared primitives, but connector mating versus closed-loop shock-absorber commissioning are materially different objectives and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Orient and feed a laminating pouch sealed-edge first, then release it to rollers; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tests thin-object orientation, square slot feeding, and release timing. Candidate tests precision tool engagement, screw/collar manipulation, socket reacquisition, and response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires a square sealed-edge bite and complete feed without an open-edge or held-pouch jam. Candidate requires two consecutive bounded mechanical impacts without bottoming, overload, rebound, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Feed orientation and roller handoff do not test adjustment, locking, or dynamic energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Drive a curved needle through two pad slots along its arc and hand it to the other hand; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires curved-path insertion, tissue-respecting motion, precise bimanual handoff, and continuous retention. Candidate requires fine hex access, captive locking, collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and iterative testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires correct entry/exit, ≥2 cm emergence, other-hand grasp, first-hand release, stability, and no tear, pad press, or drop. Candidate requires repeated safe axial stopping under numeric mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: Curved needle driving and handoff are unrelated to damper adjustment and commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Gauge seven blocks with ordered GO/NO-GO checks and sort them; candidate tunes and validates a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires repeated part alignment to two precision gaps, hands-off fit observation, classification, and sorting. Candidate requires fine tool insertion, collar locking, and iterative dynamic-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires valid ordered gauge checks and all blocks in correct trays, with strong penalties for escapes and false rejects. Candidate requires two consecutive safe stop cycles within energy, travel, velocity, force, rebound, and drift constraints.
comparisons.reason: Both use physical measurement to guide action, but dimensional classification/sorting and dynamic mechanism commissioning test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Wrap and hook a chain around a gas cylinder so it resists a pull test; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires deformable-chain routing, link selection, hook seating, cylinder stabilization, and valve avoidance. Candidate requires fine rigid-tool access, captive lock manipulation, collar adjustment, and impact-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires correct chain height/snugness, upright cylinder, hand clearance, and resistance to a 10 N pull for 2 s. Candidate requires two bounded-energy stops without bottoming, overload, rebound, damage, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Mechanical retention is a broad shared theme, but deformable chain restraint and adjustable damping are materially different mechanisms and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Play a prescribed two-hand keyboard passage with distinct dynamics and timing; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires simultaneous soft and loud key presses, sequencing, release timing, and steady tempo. Candidate requires precision hex-tool use, collar manipulation, locking, and iterative physical testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the exact note order, synchronized bass, velocity separation, even tempo, key releases, and hand clearance. Candidate requires two safe, repeatable impact stops under mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful objective, manipulation, or outcome overlap exists.

comparisons.objective: Wind back a screw-type brake piston with a two-pin tool, then seat two pads; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires aligning two tool pins, maintaining axial pressure while ratcheting, retracting a helical piston, and close-tolerance pad insertion. Candidate requires a smaller recessed bit, captive-screw manipulation, fine collar rotation, moved-socket reacquisition, and dynamic feedback tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the piston face retracted to ≤63 mm and both pads seated within tight position/orientation tolerances. Candidate requires the chosen setting retained and two impact cycles within energy, travel, force, velocity, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest general tool-adjustment record, but its tested result is screw-driven clearance creation plus pad assembly, not iterative dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Clear fragile clutter from a laptop and brace its base while opening a stiff lid; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires sequential object removal, spill avoidance, bimanual bracing, and hinge opening. Candidate requires fine hex insertion, captive locking, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires all clutter safely placed, no spill/drop/base displacement, and lid ≥90° for 1 s. Candidate requires two safe, repeatable axial stops within numeric energy, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is generic; the mechanisms and tested outcomes are otherwise unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Insert both ends of a long lamp tube into sockets and rotate it to detent-lock; candidate tunes and locks a compact damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR requires bimanual long-object support, simultaneous dual-end insertion, coordinated quarter-turn rotation, and release. Candidate requires fine hex engagement, captive-screw manipulation, small-collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and iterative response testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both pin pairs in pockets, both detents engaged near 90°, grippers clear, and 1 s stability. Candidate requires two repeated safe carriage stops with no bottoming, overload, rebound, damage, tool loss, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Both include rotation followed by locking, but dual-end lamp installation and feedback-based damper commissioning test meaningfully different physical abilities.

comparisons.objective: Land a ferruled wire in a named push-in terminal and verify retention.
comparisons.physical_skill: Flexible-wire handling and precise ferrule insertion into a spring clamp.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct terminal only, collar home, clamp engaged, and less than 1.5 mm withdrawal under a 50 N pull.
comparisons.reason: The candidate instead performs tool-mediated damper unlocking, collar adjustment, relocking, and iterative dynamic impact commissioning; terminal insertion and pull retention test a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Store glasses upright in a sliding-lid box after relocating keys, without disturbing a mug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fragile-object placement, lid pushing, and obstacle-aware sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: Keys in dish, glasses upright inside box, lid closed, arms clear, and no listed safety violation.
comparisons.reason: No fine fastener/tool engagement, adjustable mechanism, or response-based force/energy tuning is tested.

comparisons.objective: Retrofit a split cable guide and prove that a spring drawer travels freely while plugs remain seated.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual guide fitting around a cable, keeper locking, clearance management, and release actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Guide locked before release; drawer travels at least 48 mm in 3 s; sleeve clears; plugs remain seated; hands stay out during proof.
comparisons.reason: Both combine locking with a physical proof cycle, but this record tests guide selection/installation and cable clearance. The candidate tests fine hex-socket reacquisition, continuous collar tuning, and repeated impact-response commissioning under energy, travel, rebound, and force limits.

comparisons.objective: Measure a pin diameter accurately with a digital caliper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a pin square but compliant while gently closing and releasing a caliper slider.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin remains correctly located; display is within 0.05 mm of 23.40 mm; angular error at most 1 degree; jaw force at most 0.3 N.
comparisons.reason: This is compliant metrology with a displayed static dimension, not adjustment and locking of a damper followed by dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Tamp coffee level and bayonet-lock the portafilter into a group head.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual support and pressing, followed by keyed insertion and rotational locking.
comparisons.success_condition: Coffee depressed at least 6 mm while level, portafilter aligned and rotated into the lock range, then released.
comparisons.reason: Rotational locking is generic overlap only; the record lacks fine tool insertion, moving-socket reacquisition, parameter tuning, and repeated dynamic response checks.

comparisons.objective: Hold a sprung M.2 drive flat and rotate a tool-less latch over its end.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneous bimanual spring restraint and quarter-turn latch actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Drive within 2.5 degrees of flat, latch turned at least 70 degrees, both hands at least 3 cm clear, held still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: It tests simultaneous hold-and-latch coordination, whereas the candidate sequentially unlocks, withdraws a bit, tunes a collar, reacquires the moved socket, locks, and commissions dynamic damping.

comparisons.objective: Diagnose and repair a fixture that admits a backward part, then verify correct and incorrect orientations.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pin removal, guide exchange, part-number selection, precise seating, and multi-case functional verification.
comparisons.success_condition: Fault demonstrated; correct spare installed and pinned; aligned part seats; reversed part is blocked 11–13 mm high; fixture left restored.
comparisons.reason: Both include maintenance and functional verification, but this tests keyed part discrimination and guide replacement. It does not test fine torque-tool use or iterative tuning from measured impact behavior.

comparisons.objective: Load a filled syringe into a pump and bring its driver into contact without moving the plunger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre flange-slot alignment and gentle slider positioning around a sensitive plunger.
comparisons.success_condition: Syringe seated within tight pose tolerances, driver approximately flush, no disallowed plunger travel, and state held still.
comparisons.reason: This is precision loading with a no-dose constraint, not reversible fastener manipulation and iterative damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Remove snapped filament from a 3D-printer extruder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Accessing an extruder path, gripping a small broken filament, and extracting it without leaving obstruction or causing damage.
comparisons.success_condition: The obstructing filament is removed and the extruder is left clear under the record's damage constraints.
comparisons.reason: Extraction from a feed mechanism does not test adjustment-lock sequencing, moving-socket reacquisition, or dynamic impact tuning. Available rubric detail is less explicit than the candidate's force/energy thresholds but still establishes a different objective.

comparisons.objective: Hang two wine glasses upside down in an overhead channel rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thin-stem grasping, end-threading into a channel, overhead sliding, and fragile release.
comparisons.success_condition: Both feet rest on the rack lips, stems are centered, tilt is at most 5 degrees, hands are clear, and neither glass was tipped past 45 degrees.
comparisons.reason: This tests fragile high-reach insertion and hanging, not tool-driven adjustment or measured dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Use a physical mouse to drag a file into the green on-screen folder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a button press while making high-gain planar mouse motion and visually controlling a pointer.
comparisons.success_condition: File dropped in the correct folder, button released, mouse upright on its mat, fingers clear, with no wrong drop, double-click, or monitor contact.
comparisons.reason: It tests physical operation of a computer pointing device and screen feedback, not mechanical maintenance or damper response.

comparisons.objective: Release a disc from a case hub and insert it upright into a slot-loading console.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual press-and-lift release, thin-edge grasp, reorientation, and narrow-slot insertion.
comparisons.success_condition: Disc reaches the required depth upright and centered without being dropped; the drive takes it.
comparisons.reason: The press-release and insertion sequence is materially different from fine hex engagement, bounded tightening, collar tuning, and repeated impact testing.

comparisons.objective: Remove a tagged bin from the middle of a gravity lane while restraining the following bin, then close the lane.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-back and extraction under gravity, followed by controlled release and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Tagged bin rests in reject tote; next bin moves at most 2 cm before placement; remaining bins close against the stop without falls or tipping.
comparisons.reason: This tests transient gravity-flow control and material handling, not mechanism adjustment or dynamic damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Transfer at least five beads from a tray into a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and manipulate a scoop, wedge granular spheres into it, carry, and pour.
comparisons.success_condition: At least five beads rest inside the bowl for one continuous second.
comparisons.reason: Granular tool use and transfer do not exercise fastener engagement, adjustment locking, or iterative response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Hold a nail upright while another robot arm hammers it in, then retreat safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part fixturing in a shared workspace and timed withdrawal from a striking tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Nail is driven up to 4 cm; any arm-arm or hammer-arm contact forces score zero.
comparisons.reason: It tests collaborative fixturing and strike-zone clearance, not commissioning an adjustable damper.

comparisons.objective: Identify an unliftable carton, shelve the light cartons, and slide the heavy carton to a handoff zone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Test lifting, payload inference, feedback adaptation, and safe pushing/placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Light cartons rest on the shelf; the test-lifted heavy carton rests on the handoff mat; no drop, tip, or unnecessary handoff.
comparisons.reason: Although both adapt from physical feedback, this record classifies payload capacity and routes cartons rather than tuning a mechanism from measured dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Unfold, orient, and hang springy folding headphones.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual manipulation of passive hinges and an elastic segmented headband, followed by stable hanging.
comparisons.success_condition: Both fold joints open, both cushions face inward within 15 degrees, and the released headset hangs stably for 5 s.
comparisons.reason: Articulated elastic-object preparation is a different tested ability from fine tool use and impact commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Strip 10 mm of insulation using a lever-operated benchtop stripping station.
comparisons.physical_skill: Insert a cable to depth, hold a lever closed, withdraw the cable while the blades remain closed, then release.
comparisons.success_condition: Eight to twelve millimetres stripped, lever returned, and hands clear; releasing before withdrawal fails to remove the insulation.
comparisons.reason: It shares sequencing around a small cable and mechanism, but tests cut-and-pull coordination rather than adjustment, relocking, and dynamic response validation.

comparisons.objective: Install a processor by opening its socket linkage, keying and seating the chip, then closing the shield and lever.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sub-millimetre keyed placement and manipulation of an interlocked shield, lever, and catch.
comparisons.success_condition: Processor flat within 1 degree, centered within 0.8 mm, oriented within 2 degrees, shield shut, and lever secured under its catch.
comparisons.reason: This is keyed component installation and enclosure locking; it does not tune a parameter or validate repeated dynamic performance.

comparisons.objective: Fit a carriage over the open end of a T-rail and push it past a spring plunger to the stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Undercut slide-fit alignment, constrained pushing through a detent, and clean release.
comparisons.success_condition: Carriage is captured on the rail, past the plunger, within 3 mm of the stop, level, still, and released.
comparisons.reason: The record tests one-time rail insertion and detent passage. It lacks tool-mediated unlocking, iterative setting selection, and force/energy-qualified impact cycles.

comparisons.objective: Fit two beveled steel coupons for a V-groove weld.
comparisons.physical_skill: Heavy-part reorientation and precise planar alignment of bevels, ends, and root gap.
comparisons.success_condition: Both coupons flat and still, bevels opposed, 1.6–3.2 mm opening at both ends, and ends aligned within 5 mm.
comparisons.reason: Static weld fit-up is materially different from mechanical adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding-table leg, secure its brace with a sliding ring, and prove the lock under side load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulated linkage opening, sleeve/ring positioning over a knee, clearance, and load-proof sequencing.
comparisons.success_condition: Leg within 1 degree of upright, ring at least 12 mm past the knee pin, hands clear, and no more than 3 degrees folding under a 6 N test.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest functional pattern—adjust, lock, clear, and proof-load—but the tested ability is gross linkage deployment and ring locking. The candidate adds recessed hex-bit insertion, captive screw torque, withdrawal/re-engagement after collar motion, fine continuous tuning, and two energy/force/rebound-qualified impact cycles.

comparisons.objective: Release a hard drive from a spring-pin tool-less carrier and place it on an anti-static mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually deflect and hold a sprung rail while pivoting and sliding a fragile drive off retained pins.
comparisons.success_condition: Drive progresses from pin release to full removal and safe placement; broken rails, drops, or shocks permanently score zero.
comparisons.reason: The record has no spec versions in the indexed JSON; its complete body supplies the objective, staged scoring, and damage gates. Those establish spring-retainer extraction as different from damper adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Slide a booster tray onto two armrests and latch both catches at the middle notch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual wide-object rail alignment and synchronized pushing through two spring ratchets.
comparisons.success_condition: Both catches occupy notch 2, tray is flat and centered, hands clear, and the free-standing seat and tray remain stable without falls.
comparisons.reason: It tests bilateral rail/catch alignment and stopping at a discrete notch, not fine tool engagement, continuous adjustment, relocking, or response-based calibration.

comparisons.objective: Replace a printer toner cartridge and close the front door without touching the transfer roller.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large keyed-cartridge removal, guide-rail insertion and seating, door manipulation, and obstacle avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Old cartridge safely on the table, new cartridge seated in both notches, door shut, arms clear, with no printer movement, roller contact, drop, or excessive tilt.
comparisons.reason: This is component exchange and keyed rail insertion; it does not test adjustment of a retained mechanism or iterative physical response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Remove a latched EV connector, holster it, and close the port door.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a release while extracting a heavy cabled connector, reinsert it into a holster, and close a hinged door.
comparisons.success_condition: No ≥40 N latched yank or drop; connector holstered and released; door closed.
comparisons.reason: The candidate commissions a damper through fine-tool loosening, collar adjustment, relocking, and repeated dynamic impact tests. This record tests latched cable extraction and stowage, not parameter adjustment or response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Release a printed part by flexing a build plate, then bin the part and restore the plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually bend a deformable plate in the correct direction without exceeding its curvature limit.
comparisons.success_condition: Part freed and binned; plate returned flat; no kink, drop, or excessive downward displacement.
comparisons.reason: This is controlled deformable-object bending and part release. The candidate instead uses a hex bit and rotating collar to tune a rigid damper and validate dynamic stops.

comparisons.objective: Tighten a rack of pool balls and remove the triangle without disturbing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress many free-rolling objects into a tight pack and lift a surrounding frame vertically.
comparisons.success_condition: All 30 neighbor pairs within 0.5 mm, head ball within 5 mm of the spot, and no ball displaced over 3 mm during rack removal.
comparisons.reason: The record tests collective manipulation of rolling objects and disturbance-free frame removal, absent from damper adjustment and impact-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Set two forearm crutches to the same marked height and ensure both spring buttons fully engage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Depress a spring button, slide a telescoping leg through intermediate holes, and align the button with a target hole.
comparisons.success_condition: Both buttons fully protrude through the marked holes; crutches released, stable, and not dropped.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve adjustment and positive locking, this record tests button-controlled telescoping alignment to a known hole. The candidate tests tool-mediated rotary adjustment followed by iterative dynamic-response validation.

comparisons.objective: Install a carriage on a linear rail and push it through a detent to an end stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a close-fitting profile, start a linear insertion, maintain squareness, and overcome a spring plunger.
comparisons.success_condition: Carriage seated on the rail, past the restored plunger, against the stop, with the rail not substantially displaced.
comparisons.reason: This is precision profile insertion with detent engagement. It does not test loosening and relocking an adjustment mechanism or tuning from measured impact response.

comparisons.objective: Release two simultaneous latches, remove a lid, and place it beside its case.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually retract opposed spring latches while lifting a constrained lid.
comparisons.success_condition: Both latches released together; lid lifted clear and placed flat; case remains substantially fixed.
comparisons.reason: The defining ability is simultaneous bimanual latch actuation during removal, unlike sequential tool use, collar rotation, and guarded dynamic testing in the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Rotate a long parcel in confined space and place it lengthwise in a bay.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply coordinated opposing pushes to rotate a large object without colliding with nearby obstacles, then translate it into a narrow entrance.
comparisons.success_condition: Parcel released flat, correctly oriented, inside the bay and at the stop; neighboring boxes and lateral limits undisturbed.
comparisons.reason: This record tests large-object planar manipulation under clearance constraints, not fine tool engagement or commissioning a dynamic energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Pour the contents of a heavy pot into a bowl and return the pot to the stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually lift, carry, and tilt a two-handled vessel while controlling granular contents.
comparisons.success_condition: Required contents delivered with limited spill; pot returned upright to the stove without low-altitude tipping.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is coordinated load bearing and controlled pouring. The candidate instead tests small-feature tool use and iterative mechanical tuning.

comparisons.objective: Diagnose a failed module from a blink code, replace it, and confirm recovery.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a diagnostic button, count a temporal code, extract the identified module, insert a spare, and rerun diagnosis.
comparisons.success_condition: Only the failed module replaced, all sockets seated, confirmation lamp steady green, fixture stable, and hands released.
comparisons.reason: Both include a test-adjust-retest sequence, but this record meaningfully tests temporal fault identification and keyed module exchange. The candidate tests continuous damper-setting adjustment based on physical impact response, with tool relocking and force/travel limits.

comparisons.objective: Cap and shake a cocktail shaker, then return it upright without losing contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Use one hand to retain a cap while the other supports a vessel through repeated high-amplitude reversals.
comparisons.success_condition: Capped shaker tipped and reversed at least four times, all beads retained, and tin returned upright.
