comparisons.reason: This is bimanual closure retention during dynamic shaking, not fine adjustment, tool reacquisition, or impact-stop commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Insert a circuit board into an antistatic bag and place the bag in a crate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold open/stabilize a compliant bag while feeding a flat rigid board into its cavity.
comparisons.success_condition: Board fully inside near the closed end; bag released flat inside the crate; neither item dropped.
comparisons.reason: The record tests rigid-into-compliant insertion and packaging. It shares only generic alignment and bimanual stabilization with the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Fit a rubber stopper onto a glass tube to a specified depth without unsafe loading.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support fragile tubing close to the work point while twisting and advancing a tight stopper.
comparisons.success_condition: Stopper at least 12 mm down and released; unsafe unsupported twisting, representing tube breakage, scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests supported press-and-twist insertion on a fragile assembly. The candidate uses a hex tool and collar to tune a damper, then validates dynamic performance.

comparisons.objective: Replace a worn soft-gripper finger and refit its plate and screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove and bin a flexible finger, seat a replacement, position a fork plate, and place three M3 screws into small holes.
comparisons.success_condition: New finger and plates correctly seated, all three screws placed, worn part binned, good finger undisturbed, and components released and still.
comparisons.reason: This is multi-part disassembly/reassembly with repeated small-part placement. It does not require parameter tuning from measured machine response or guarded impact cycling.

comparisons.objective: Open a crown-capped bottle using a fixed opener and place it on a coaster.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align the cap edge with a fixed tooth and use a controlled bottle stroke to lever the cap off.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap removed by the opener; bottle remains within tilt limits and is released upright and still on the coaster.
comparisons.reason: The record tests workpiece-to-fixed-tool alignment and prying, not adjustment and relocking of a mechanism followed by quantitative dynamic trials.

comparisons.objective: Hang two parts on separate continuously moving conveyor hooks before a deadline.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time grasp, eye-to-hook insertion, and release against moving targets without impeding them.
comparisons.success_condition: Each part hangs freely on its own hook for the final second before the hook crosses the mark; hooks remain on schedule.
comparisons.reason: This tests time-critical insertion onto moving hooks. The candidate's moving response occurs only after adjustment, in a separate guarded impact fixture.

comparisons.objective: Fit a servo horn onto a splined shaft at the indexed zero orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely align bore, shaft, tilt, and angular index before press-fitting onto discrete splines.
comparisons.success_condition: Horn seated flush within tight positional and angular tolerances, released and still; wrong final tooth scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This is indexed spline alignment and press-fit assembly. The candidate's collar rotation selects a setting and requires dynamic-response verification rather than discrete tooth alignment.

comparisons.objective: Reconnect and tighten a car battery's positive cable clamp safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seat and orient a clamp, engage a wrench on a nut, tighten through a bounded angle, then remove the tool from the battery.
comparisons.success_condition: Clamp seated, centered, square, tightened 75–360 degrees, lug aligned, wrench and hands cleared, and battery unmoved.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest tool-tightening record, but its tested outcome is terminal-clamp installation and safe wrench clearance. It lacks collar adjustment, socket reacquisition after collar motion, and iterative impact-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Insert a headrest into two sleeves and lock it at the lowest notch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually align two long posts, insert them together, and manage a spring pawl without forcing it.
comparisons.success_condition: Both posts inserted, lowest notch engaged, headrest released and still; drops or forced pawl passage score zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests dual-post insertion and notch engagement, not fine rotary tuning with a tool or validation under repeated dynamic loads.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a biased angle gauge against a reference and level an adjustable platform.
comparisons.physical_skill: Move a gauge between reference and work surfaces, infer bias, and iteratively actuate leveling buttons.
comparisons.success_condition: Reference and platform readings obtained hands-clear; true platform tilt within 0.15 degrees with penalties for inefficient button presses.
comparisons.reason: Both test calibration-informed iterative adjustment, but this record's defining ability is reference-based metrology and button-actuated leveling. The candidate requires fine hex/collar manipulation, relocking, guarded impact cycling, and force/travel/rebound limits.

comparisons.objective: Install foam protectors onto two bare picture-frame corners.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align compliant pockets with two frame edges and push them fully home without shifting the supported frame.
comparisons.success_condition: Both protectors seated, square, level, squeezed onto the frame, released and still; frame and existing protectors remain undisturbed.
comparisons.reason: This is compliant two-axis press-fit packaging. It does not test adjustable-mechanism locking or response-driven commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Serve exactly one meatball without utensil cross-contamination.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scoop, transport, and release a rolling food item using the correct utensil while avoiding prohibited contacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one meatball delivered by actual scoop support, released on the plate and uncontaminated; spills, direct robot contact, or contamination fail.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is contamination-aware utensil handling and food transfer, wholly different from mechanical adjustment and impact testing.

comparisons.objective: Perform a three-stage serial dilution and return the pipette.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequence pipette aspiration/dispensing across cups while preventing backward contamination.
comparisons.success_condition: Three target concentrations achieved in order, no forbidden re-entry or misplaced dispensing, and empty pipette returned and released.
comparisons.reason: This tests ordered liquid-transfer logic and contamination control; the candidate tests physical tool engagement, mechanical setting, and dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Remove a flashlight battery for recycling after unscrewing its threaded tail cap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a cylindrical body, follow a collision-modeled thread through about one turn, set down the cap, and tip out the cell.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap genuinely unscrewed and placed, battery in the bin, flashlight returned and released; forced thread separation or dropped parts fail.
comparisons.reason: Both include bimanual rotary manipulation, but this record tests threaded disassembly and gravity-assisted extraction. The candidate loosens only a captive lock, adjusts and relocks a collar, then tunes dynamic stopping performance.

comparisons.objective: Release a cordless-drill battery and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the drill while simultaneously squeezing two opposed buttons and sliding the battery along its rails.
comparisons.success_condition: Both buttons actuated together, pack fully removed and released flat in the tray, drill remains near its start, and nothing falls.
comparisons.reason: This tests simultaneous dual-button release plus linear pack extraction, not fine-tool locking or iterative damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Measure a wooden bar and enter its length on a physical calculator.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate a spring-return tape, visually read a scale, retract/place the tape, and press calculator keys.
comparisons.success_condition: First submitted integer equals the bar's longest dimension within 120 seconds.
comparisons.reason: This record tests physical measurement, visual scale interpretation, and data entry. It does not manipulate or commission an adjustable mechanical component.

comparisons.objective: Remove a press-fit paint-tin lid and place it on the table; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through dynamic testing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated screwdriver prying and tin reorientation versus fine hex-socket engagement, collar adjustment, relocking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid fully separated and safely placed versus two force- and travel-compliant stops without bottoming, rebound, overload, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Tool use and rotation are generic shared primitives; the mechanisms and tested outcomes differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Mount, position, and tighten a DIN-rail end bracket; candidate tunes a mounted damper's dynamic response.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual rail stabilization, bracket hooking/sliding, and slotted-screw tightening versus captive setscrew release, fine collar tuning, socket reacquisition, and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket seated flush and tightened to 0.5 Nm while the rail remains fixed versus two safe repeatable carriage stops within energy, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Both include screw-tool manipulation, but only the candidate tests iterative damping adjustment from measured impacts.

comparisons.objective: Measure a training doll by straightening its sprung legs and closing a footboard; candidate commissions an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained bimanual restraint of compliant legs while sliding a measuring stop versus precision hex-tool and collar manipulation followed by dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Legs straight and footboard left at a valid length reading versus repeatable non-bottoming stops within specified physical limits.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests tuning and retention of an energy absorber, not compliant-body positioning for measurement.

comparisons.objective: Cut a cable tie from a bundle without damaging cables; candidate adjusts and validates a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place sprung cutters beside the tie head and close them with damage avoidance versus engage a recessed hex socket, rotate a fine collar, relock it, and cycle a carriage.
comparisons.success_condition: Tie severed and removed with no cable nick versus two safe stops with bounded travel, forces, rebound, and setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Damage-sensitive cutting and dynamic damper commissioning require different mechanisms and abilities.

comparisons.objective: Saw a marked 45-degree mitre while holding moulding against a fence; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual workpiece restraint and repeated guided sawing versus small-tool insertion, collar adjustment, socket reacquisition, and guarded test actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Moulding cut through at the marked angle and tool/workpiece cleared versus two compliant impact cycles without bottoming or limit violations.
comparisons.reason: Shared iterative motion does not equate guided cutting with closed-loop impact-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Riddle sparkling-wine bottles by controlled one-eighth turns in a rack; candidate commissions an industrial shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp and incrementally rotate bottles while maintaining rack placement versus loosen-adjust-relock manipulation and dynamic carriage testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Required bottles remain correctly turned and seated versus two consecutive safe stops with retained collar setting.
comparisons.reason: The bottle task tests indexed container rotation, not tool-mediated adjustment of energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Tear the perforated front panel from a shelf-ready can tray; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Initiate and propagate a controlled perforation tear around packaged cans versus fine socket engagement, collar rotation, relocking, and response-driven iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Front panel removed along its perforation without disrupting the tray contents versus compliant stops meeting travel, force, rebound, and drift constraints.
comparisons.reason: Controlled package tearing and damper commissioning have different physical mechanisms and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Open a beverage can using its recessed stay-on tab; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pinch and lift a low-profile tab until the scored seal breaks versus hex-bit insertion, bounded torque, fine collar adjustment, and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Can seal opened with tab appropriately actuated versus two safe repeatable carriage stops and a locked, stable setting.
comparisons.reason: Both require small-feature manipulation, but the candidate additionally tests adjustable damping under dynamic load.

comparisons.objective: Fit a hose over a barb and secure it with a clamp; candidate tunes an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align and push a hose onto a barb, position a clamp, and tighten it versus release and reacquire a moving setscrew socket around fine collar adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Hose fully seated and clamp correctly located and tightened versus repeatable non-bottoming impact stops within force and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Fastener tightening is only a shared primitive; hose assembly does not test response-based damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Reset tongue-and-groove pliers from the first to the fifth groove; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open the pliers past their release angle, translate the joint, and close it into a groove versus hex-tool manipulation, fine collar tuning, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Pliers locked in groove five and resting untouched versus two safe dynamic stops with the collar relocked and stable.
comparisons.reason: Indexed joint reconfiguration differs from iterative adjustment based on measured energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Dry-fit and center a slip coupling across a drain-pipe repair joint; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support a sagging pipe in coaxial alignment while sliding a close-clearance sleeve versus manipulate a small lock and collar, then operate a test fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: Both pipe ends aligned and inserted to balanced witness-mark depths versus two cycles satisfying travel, force, rebound, and retention limits.
comparisons.reason: Close-clearance coaxial assembly is materially different from dynamic response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Join two boards evenly on three dowels; candidate commissions an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually align three simultaneous pin/socket pairs and press without wedging versus precision tool insertion, collar adjustment, relocking, and test iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Board seam fully seated, flush, flat, and released versus two non-bottoming stops with bounded forces and no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Multi-pin insertion and even seating do not test adjustable energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Hook and snap a module onto a DIN rail; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient a module, hook one rail lip, swing it in, and deflect a spring latch versus hex-bit seating, fine collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and dynamic cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Module squarely mounted with its latch engaged versus two safe, repeatable impact stops and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: The rail task tests hook-and-latch mounting, not response-driven damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Hold a marked part at height while closing a bench vise; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually support and align a workpiece while rotating a vise knob to clamp it versus loosen a captive lock, adjust a small collar, relock, clear, and test.
comparisons.success_condition: Part clamped upright with its line at jaw height versus two force- and travel-compliant stops without drift or damage.
comparisons.reason: Knob rotation and clamping are generic overlap; only the candidate requires iterative dynamic-response validation.

comparisons.objective: Plant and support a seedling while pouring soil around it; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a top-heavy object upright while tipping and distributing many loose clods versus fine tool/collar manipulation and controlled carriage cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Seedling stands independently, upright and centered with sufficient soil versus repeatable non-bottoming stops within mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: Granular support construction and energy-absorber commissioning test unrelated abilities.

comparisons.objective: Post a packet fully through a spring-flap slot; candidate commissions an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and push an object through a one-way constrained opening without following it inside versus engage, adjust, and relock a small mechanism before guarded testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Packet entirely inside and stationary with flap shut versus two compliant impact cycles without overload, rebound, bottoming, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Constrained posting through a flap is not adjustment or dynamic validation of a damper.

comparisons.objective: Align a sagging replacement pipe and slide a repair coupling across its joint; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual coaxial pipe support and sleeve translation versus precision hex-tool use, fine collar rotation, relocking, and iterative physical testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Coupling centered with both pipes inserted and aligned after release versus two safe carriage stops satisfying force, travel, rebound, and retention thresholds.
comparisons.reason: Both involve industrial maintenance, but the tested manipulation and outcome are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Feed springy filament into a narrow 3D-printer inlet; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually straighten, align, and insert a flexible filament versus manipulate a rigid captive lock and collar and evaluate impact response.
comparisons.success_condition: Filament inserted at least 20 mm, released, and still versus two safe repeatable damper cycles with a stable locked setting.
comparisons.reason: Flexible linear insertion differs from rigid adjustment plus dynamic energy-management testing.

comparisons.objective: Move a heavy carton onto a low platform using edge placement and pushing; candidate tunes a compact damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manage a large load through tilt, edge support, and whole-body pushing versus millimetric tool engagement, collar adjustment, relocking, and guarded actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton securely supported on the platform without loss or unsafe motion versus two bounded impact stops without bottoming, overload, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Heavy-object levering and fine commissioning test meaningfully different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Push rejects off a moving production line at the correct time; candidate commissions an axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time contact with moving objects and redirect them from a conveyor versus small-tool manipulation and iterative adjustment from measured carriage behavior.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified rejects removed while acceptable items remain and line hazards are avoided versus two consecutive safe stops within explicit dynamic limits.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve dynamic equipment, sorting moving items does not tune or lock an energy absorber.

comparisons.objective: Identify a leaking cable core using a hand-crank insulation tester; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place electrical probes, operate a hand crank, and interpret comparative readings versus insert a hex bit, adjust and lock a collar, and iterate physical impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct faulty core identified from valid tester operation without unsafe contact versus two compliant carriage stops within force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Both use test-act-interpret sequencing, but one diagnoses insulation while the other physically changes and validates damping.

comparisons.objective: Remove a binder clip before feeding invoices into a shredder; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pinch a sprung clip off a stack, handle paper, and feed it while avoiding a jam versus precision lock/collar manipulation and guarded carriage cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Invoices shredded with clip removed and no hand/clip entering the slot versus two safe repeatable stops with no overload, bottoming, or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Safety sequencing is shared only generically; the mechanisms and tested outcomes differ.

comparisons.objective: Secure a carton to a cart with a stretched bungee and verify retention; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stretch an elastic cord and hook both ends against tension versus fine hex-socket engagement, collar rotation, relocking, and test-control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Hooks remain home and carton retained through a cart motion test versus two force- and travel-compliant carriage stops with no collar drift.
comparisons.reason: Both include post-manipulation physical testing, but elastic restraint assembly is not adjustable damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Safely replace a control cassette supplied by independent mains and backup feeds; candidate commissions a mechanical shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Verify live state, isolate two feeds, prove dead, remove/install a cassette, close a guard, and restore power versus loosen-adjust-relock fine mechanics and tune from impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Cassette replaced with the bus proven below 1 V and supplies restored only after hands clear versus two safe non-bottoming stops within energy, velocity, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Safe service sequencing and guarded control use overlap generically, but cassette replacement and damper tuning test different physical abilities.

comparisons.objective: Hold a notice at a marked line and pin it to a tilted cork board; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually position a sliding card and drive a small pin with sufficient insertion force versus seat a hex bit, tune a collar, reacquire the socket, and relock it.
comparisons.success_condition: Notice hangs straight at the line from a seated pin after release versus two consecutive compliant stops with bounded forces and retained adjustment.
comparisons.reason: Small-part insertion and force control are generic commonalities; pinning a card does not test dynamic damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Place a baby bottle upright in a pre-warmed water bath while avoiding microwave activation and nipple submersion.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe bottle lifting and upright placement into an open pan; no tool seating, locking, or dynamic damper tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle supported near the bath center, sufficiently immersed but neck clear, released and stationary; heat transfer is not simulated.
comparisons.reason: The candidate commissions a shock absorber through fine-tool locking, collar adjustment, and repeated impact-response testing. This record tests safe method selection and container placement.

comparisons.objective: Lift a deformable cord, move a cart underneath without contact, then restore and release the cord.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual slack management: hold a flexible obstacle clear while sliding another object beneath it.
comparisons.success_condition: Cart crosses and finishes past the line without touching or leaving the table; cord is returned near its original line and released.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is coordinated deformable-object clearance, not captive-fastener manipulation, indexed adjustment, or commissioning from dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Recycle scrap notepads while leaving a private letter untouched.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic object selection followed by ordinary rigid pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Both scraps rest in the bin; moving the private letter into the bin or off the table invalidates the result.
comparisons.reason: This tests privacy-aware selection, whereas the candidate tests precision maintenance and closed-loop damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Retract an exposed utility-knife blade before stowing the knife.
comparisons.physical_skill: Slide a small control while maintaining clearance from a hazardous edge, then grasp and place the tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Blade fully retracted and knife released in the tray, with no finger near the exposed blade and no unsafe intermediate rest.
comparisons.reason: Although both require safety sequencing around a small mechanism, this record tests hazard recognition and linear blade retraction, not socket reacquisition, collar locking, or impact tuning.

comparisons.objective: Open two hinged forceps and load them flat and unstacked into a sterilizer basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Articulate free hinged tools, preserve their opening during transfer, and arrange them in a basket.
comparisons.success_condition: Both forceps released, still, flat, wholly in the basket, and at least 15 degrees open.
comparisons.reason: The meaningful ability is maintaining articulated instrument state during placement; it does not test threaded locking or response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Feed a hex shaft through two aligned bearings with usable projection at both ends.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-part pose alignment, close-clearance insertion, and incremental regrasping through two apertures.
comparisons.success_condition: Shaft crosses both bearings, projects at least 1 cm beyond each outside face, and becomes still.
comparisons.reason: This is a dual-aperture insertion task. The candidate's brief hex-bit insertion is only a generic primitive within a substantially different adjust-lock-test procedure.

comparisons.objective: Free a fused print-in-place hinge by repeated gentle rocking, then swing it open without breaking it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cyclic bounded-force articulation that progressively releases modeled adhesion before a large final rotation.
comparisons.success_condition: Leaf remains attached, reaches at least 120 degrees, and is still; excessive torque or displacement constitutes snapping.
comparisons.reason: Both involve iteration, but this record tests progressive breakaway through alternating motion. The candidate iterates a setting based on measured carriage impacts and then locks it.

comparisons.objective: Erect a folding produce crate and latch all four sprung corners.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered wall articulation, bimanual bracing and pulling through spring catches, followed by release.
comparisons.success_condition: Four corners latched, walls vertical, base flat, crate still, and both grippers clear.
comparisons.reason: This tests multibody erection and four mechanical latches, not precision screw/collar adjustment or dynamic stop commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Make a chainsaw safe for carrying by engaging its chain brake and fitting the bar cover.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a detented hinged guard and align/slide a long cover over the bar while avoiding chain contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Brake engaged, cover over at least 95% of the bar within alignment tolerances, saw not displaced, arms clear, state held two seconds.
comparisons.reason: The safety sequence and cover insertion differ materially from loosening, adjusting, relocking, and experimentally tuning a damper.

comparisons.objective: Seat and quarter-turn a Sankey coupler on a keg, then lower its handle to drive the probe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tight axial alignment, bayonet engagement, rotation under lugs, and ordered over-center handle actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Coupler caught and turned about 85–90 degrees before handle engagement, probe substantially inserted, keg/lines undamaged, hands clear and mechanism still.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared align-rotate-lock sequence, but it tests bayonet coupling and ordered probe actuation. The candidate additionally requires fine setscrew tooling, moving-socket reacquisition, and tuning from repeated impact measurements.

comparisons.objective: Insert a long board behind two boards already leaning in a rack without removing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: One hand maintains a temporary gap while the other inserts a long rigid object, then restores the supported stack.
comparisons.success_condition: All boards remain on the rack floor; the long board is at the back and the short boards lean onto it after release.
comparisons.reason: This tests bimanual gap maintenance and constrained placement, not maintenance-tool control or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Instill exactly one eye drop into a drawn-down lower-lid pocket and return the bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Light-contact lid displacement combined with precise nozzle aiming and tightly controlled squeeze force/duration.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one modeled drop lands in the pocket, tip never contacts the face, force limits are respected, lid closes, and bottle is released on the tray.
comparisons.reason: Its central ability is delicate bimanual dosing near a compliant anatomical target; the candidate tests mechanical adjustment and impact response.

comparisons.objective: Progressively seat a fixed-end power cord along an entire curved channel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential deformable routing and pressing along a bend without pulling out the anchored end.
comparisons.success_condition: All eight channel sections contain the cord below the lip; channel and source box remain fixed.
comparisons.reason: Progressive cable routing is meaningfully different from fine-tool engagement, locking, and quantitative damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Load two equal tubes into opposite centrifuge-rotor pockets.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick, orient, and insert two cylinders into separated pockets while applying an implicit balance rule.
comparisons.success_condition: Both tubes are seated in pockets 180 degrees apart; an unbalanced pair scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This tests balanced multi-object insertion rather than adjustment of a mechanical response under repeated physical trials.

comparisons.objective: Transfer sample into acceptable tubes and move matching checklist tabs without falsifying an unacceptable fourth sample.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated pipette handling, dose transfer, and paired physical record actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Three tubes are filled to their marks and correctly ticked; the fourth remains empty and unticked; water or a false tick invalidates the trial.
comparisons.reason: The record tests sample integrity and fill/record correspondence, not socket manipulation or damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Pack selected boxes into a carton according to a printed two-layer plan while excluding distractors.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plan interpretation, layered placement, and contact pushing to meet tight face-position tolerances.
comparisons.success_condition: Four specified boxes match planned faces within 5 mm and two excluded boxes remain outside the carton.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained packing and visual-plan execution, with no adjustable mechanism or response-based calibration.

comparisons.objective: Raise a flat wide box onto a riser and tip it into a narrow slot standing on edge.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual squeeze lift, ledge-assisted reorientation, and constrained placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Box stands released in the slot on a small face with its long dimension near vertical and remains still.
comparisons.reason: The task tests whole-object reorientation through environmental leverage, unlike precision damper adjustment and testing.

comparisons.objective: Carry a loose three-box stack to a shelf in one trip without separating or destabilizing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual squeeze transport of the bottom box while preserving an unsupported stack through lift, carry, and set-down.
comparisons.success_condition: Stack never breaks specified separation/offset/tilt limits and ends level, supported, centered, and released on the shelf.
comparisons.reason: This tests stability-preserving transport of multiple loose bodies, not mechanism commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Drain water from a pan through a lid held ajar while retaining dumplings, then return the pan to the stove.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual lid-gap regulation and coordinated pan tipping with particulate retention.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan ends upright on the stove, sufficient water beads reach the sink, and all dumplings remain in the pan.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is coordinated pouring and retention. It shares force coordination only at a generic level with the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Sort colored cubes from a shared bin while yielding both arms during a person's timed incursions.
comparisons.physical_skill: Human-aware interruption, spatial separation, coordinated retreat, resumption, and pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: No gripper enters the bin or approaches within 10 cm while the hand is present; cubes finish on matching mats.
comparisons.reason: This evaluates dynamic shared-space safety and work resumption, not mechanical calibration. The body supplies the main zero/full rubric despite having no indexed spec versions.

comparisons.objective: Align a passive service slider's hidden index to an interior mark using an inspection view, then release it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Occlusion-aware visual servoing and contact adjustment of a passive slider through a service opening.
comparisons.success_condition: Released slider remains still with sub-millimeter final alignment; roof contact is rejected.
comparisons.reason: Both concern adjustment, but this record tests direct hidden visual alignment of one slider, while the candidate infers a damper setting from repeated dynamic impacts and secures it with a captive screw. The record body omits the complete partial-credit thresholds, but that omission does not create a plausible duplicate.

comparisons.objective: Pick four moving parts from two lanes before their different deadlines and place them in a bin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deadline-aware interception, grasping from servo-driven carriers, and rapid transfer without staging.
comparisons.success_condition: Each cube goes directly from its carrier to the bin before passing under the cover; all four still in the bin gives full credit.
comparisons.reason: This tests temporal scheduling and moving-object interception rather than fine maintenance manipulation or physical-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Pass a tall canister over a shelf fence under low overhead clearance and stand it upright behind the fence.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tilt-to-clear insertion, base placement, and in-place reorientation under a height constraint.
comparisons.success_condition: Canister is released, upright on its base behind the fence, inside side bounds, and still.
comparisons.reason: This is constrained whole-object insertion and stand-up, not an adjustable-device commissioning procedure.

comparisons.objective: Pour mixed coins from a jar and sort pennies and quarters into separate frames.
comparisons.physical_skill: Controlled rigid-body pouring followed by separating and pushing thin objects across a surface.
comparisons.success_condition: Each of ten coins lies wholly in its denomination's assigned frame; credit is per correctly sorted coin.
comparisons.reason: The ability tested is granular unloading and denomination sorting, with no mechanical locking or feedback calibration.

comparisons.objective: Cue a record by placing the stylus in the gap before track three.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp a 5 mm finger lift, follow a hinged tonearm arc, count visual track gaps, and lower the stylus gently and precisely.
comparisons.success_condition: Stylus rests in the 109–113 mm target gap, arm still and hands clear; excessive touchdown speed or post-contact sliding permanently invalidates the trial.
comparisons.reason: This tests gentle articulated placement onto a visually selected narrow target. It has no setscrew/collar manipulation or iterative dynamic-response criterion; its body provides the rubric despite no indexed spec versions.

comparisons.objective: Dock and latch a laptop onto a port replicator; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber through repeated impact tests.
comparisons.physical_skill: Large-object bimanual leveling, connector alignment and symmetric latch engagement versus fine hex-bit insertion, captive-screw torque, collar adjustment and response-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Laptop must be level, seated on the connector and latched without dropping or later removal; candidate requires two safe cycles within travel, energy, velocity, force, rebound and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Both involve alignment and latching, but the tested mechanisms and outcomes differ materially. This record has no separate spec version; its body supplies the rubric.

comparisons.objective: Cock a sprung phone holder, place a phone and trigger its arms; candidate adjusts and validates a hydraulic damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Opening coupled arms and centering a phone against a trigger versus tool-mediated screw release, fine collar rotation, socket reacquisition and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Phone must be edge-clamped, stable and released without a fall or glass-face strike; candidate instead requires repeatable axial stopping under explicit force and travel limits.
comparisons.reason: The shared spring/latch and release primitives do not test damper commissioning or measured dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Release an anti-theft tag clutch with a magnetic detacher and pull its pin; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Precisely seat a detacher while pulling a pin bimanually versus insert and withdraw a hex bit, rotate a collar, relock it and tune from impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Clutch must be released before extracting the pin, followed by hands-off separation; candidate requires two compliant physical impact cycles with no drift or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both use gated release followed by manipulation, but one tests clutch release and pin extraction while the other tests adjustment retention and dynamic damping.

comparisons.objective: Refit a spring-plunger window screen into top and bottom channels; candidate tunes an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual large-frame lifting, plunger compression, swinging and channel seating versus fine tool use and iterative force-response adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Screen must be fitted, centered, planar, still and released without dropping or forcing the frame; candidate instead passes through bounded repeated impacts.
comparisons.reason: Spring compression is generic; the record tests constrained large-frame insertion rather than commissioning a dissipative mechanism.

comparisons.objective: Intercept and stop a rolling bottle before it falls; candidate adjusts a damper and evaluates carriage stopping.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fast moving-object interception and gentle arrest versus deliberate small-tool manipulation and iterative mechanism tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle must become still on the worktop without ever crossing an edge; candidate requires two axial carriage stops without bottoming, overload, rebound or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Both concern stopping motion, but bottle interception tests reactive catching, not adjustment and validation of a shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Route a lamp cable into a holder while keeping the entire cable clear of a hot plate; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-cable routing and plug placement under a keep-out constraint versus rigid fine-tool engagement, collar rotation and impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug must be seated and released while the cable remains outside the hazard and satisfies final clearance; candidate uses force, energy, travel, rebound and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful mechanism or tested ability overlaps beyond generic placement and safety constraints.

comparisons.objective: Pull cable from a channel to a ruler mark without over-pulling; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable extraction, handover and visual length control versus captive setscrew operation, fine rotary adjustment and dynamic-response iteration.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable end must finish near 30 cm, straight and released, never beyond 35 cm; candidate must produce two compliant impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both require bounded adjustment, but cable length metering does not test tool-mediated mechanical commissioning or damping behavior.

comparisons.objective: Select the fitting pin and seat it fully in a fixture hole; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Part discrimination, arm-to-arm relay and peg insertion versus recessed hex engagement, bounded torque, collar manipulation and repeated response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct pin must reach the hole floor upright and remain still; candidate requires locked adjustment plus two force- and travel-compliant impacts.
comparisons.reason: Fine alignment is shared only as a generic primitive; the functional abilities and outcomes are different.

comparisons.objective: Remove a rejected tote while restraining a gravity-fed queue, then release the queue; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual load restraint and tote transfer versus small-tool insertion, torque, fine rotation and iterative impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Red tote must reach the bin while the queue moves no more than 2 cm, then grey totes advance to the stop; candidate requires two bounded axial stops.
comparisons.reason: The record tests coordinated material handling under gravity, not mechanism adjustment or damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Tension, pluck and release a chalk line to make one straight mark; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tension maintenance and controlled transverse release versus fine screw/collar manipulation and feedback-based tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: One print must pass close to the mark with limited bow and the reel returned; candidate passes on repeated dynamic carriage behavior within mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic release and force control are generic similarities, but the measured ability and outcome are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Rotate moving cartons so labels face a fixed scanner; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed interception and in-place reorientation of moving parcels versus tool-mediated unlocking, rotary adjustment, relocking and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Each carton must remain upright on its carrier, be released and face the scanner at the gate; candidate requires two safe, repeatable stops.
comparisons.reason: The record tests conveyor timing and orientation, not mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Singulate three touching parcels on a running belt before a scanner; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed parcel spacing and temporary lifting constrained over a moving belt versus fine tool use and response-driven adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Both inter-parcel gaps must be at least 5 cm at the scanner without off-belt or stacking violations; candidate uses impact energy, travel, force, rebound and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful duplicate ability exists beyond manipulation under temporal and safety constraints.

comparisons.objective: Light a Bunsen burner with a striker and gas tap, then leave it safely burning; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tap rotation, striker positioning and squeezing with hazardous sequencing versus hex-bit torque, collar rotation and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Burner must light without exceeding the unlit-gas limit, with striker returned and controls released; candidate requires two compliant carriage cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both enforce safe sequencing around controls, but the mechanisms, actions and physical outcomes are different.

comparisons.objective: Clip a condenser onto a still head; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aligning laboratory glassware and engaging a retaining clip versus recessed tool engagement, screw torque, fine collar rotation and dynamic tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Condenser must be correctly seated and retained without damaging the apparatus; candidate requires a locked setting and two safe axial stops.
comparisons.reason: Generic alignment and retention do not make glassware assembly a duplicate of damper adjustment and performance validation.

comparisons.objective: Use a stud-layout jig to establish or place a repeated construction layout; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Jig positioning and repeated spatial layout/placement versus fine hex-tool operation, collar adjustment and iterative impact-response control.
comparisons.success_condition: The record evaluates correct jig-derived spacing or placement; candidate evaluates locked adjustment and repeated force-bounded stopping. Exact numeric layout thresholds are record-specific and immaterial to this clearly unrelated objective.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities differ materially despite both using a fixture.

comparisons.objective: Operate a cup sealer to apply a proper seal; candidate adjusts and validates a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cup/film alignment and sealer actuation versus captive-screw manipulation, collar tuning and guarded dynamic cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup must finish acceptably sealed without spill, misalignment or unsafe operation; candidate must stop a carriage twice within travel, force, rebound and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Machine operation is generic; sealing quality does not test adjustable damping or tool-mediated commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Hang a cable between two hooks with a specified sag; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable routing, hooking and tension/sag control versus rigid fine-tool insertion, torque and iterative rotary tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable must remain on both hooks with sag in the required range and be released; candidate requires two compliant impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve tuning a measured physical state, but cable geometry and damping response are different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Lay a cable in a figure-eight around two posts; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual deformable routing, crossing management and placement around posts versus small-tool use and dynamic-response commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable must form the required figure-eight and remain properly placed/released; candidate passes only through locked, safe repeated axial stops.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful mechanism or outcome overlap exists beyond generic manipulation.

comparisons.objective: Hold a cord taut and sever it safely with a knife; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tensioning and controlled cutting with hand/blade separation versus hex-bit insertion, bounded screw torque, collar rotation and testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord must be cut while held, away from hand and anchor, with knife safely set down; candidate requires two force- and travel-compliant impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve force control and safe sequencing, but cutting a tensioned cord is a materially different ability.

comparisons.objective: Move a pot off a burner and switch the burner off; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hot-object transfer and safety-control actuation versus precision fastener/collar manipulation and iterative impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Pot must be stable on the plate and burner switch off, with failure for a fallen or tipped pot; candidate must achieve repeatable bounded stopping.
comparisons.reason: The common control-actuation and safety elements are generic and do not establish overlap.

comparisons.objective: Reject an expired analyser kit into a tray and call a supervisor rather than loading it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-aware object sorting and button actuation versus fine mechanical adjustment, tool reacquisition and physical response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Expired kit must never enter the analyser bay; full success is kit in the grey tray and supervisor called. Candidate uses dynamic mechanical limits and repeated cycles.
comparisons.reason: This is a safety-policy compliance task, not dexterous mechanism commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Grate cheese while stabilizing a box grater, then leave a safe end state; candidate tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization plus repeated force-bearing strokes versus fine socket engagement, bounded torque, collar rotation and response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Latest versions require at least 5 g-equivalent grated under at least 3 N valid downstrokes, with grater standing and tools released; candidate requires two safe carriage impacts.
comparisons.reason: Both include contact-force control and iteration, but abrasion/grating is a materially different tested ability from damping commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Wait for a printer bed to cool, remove a used plate level and install a clean one; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual flat-plate transport, sequencing and placement while retaining a loose print versus precision hex/collar manipulation and impact tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Plates must not move early or drop; print remains on the used plate and clean plate finishes flat on the bed. Candidate instead requires bounded repeated stops.
comparisons.reason: Safe sequencing is shared, but plate exchange and damper commissioning test different physical abilities.

comparisons.objective: Wipe an entire monitor lead and end pieces outward without backtracking; candidate adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable-cord tensioning, sliding pinch, role switching and one-way surface coverage versus fine tool alignment, torque, collar rotation and dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: All cord marks and both end bodies must be wiped once in the allowed direction, then laid on the drape; candidate requires two compliant impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: No meaningful overlap exists beyond bimanual force control.

comparisons.objective: Cut three hedge shoots with two-handed shears while sparing flowers; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual articulated-tool control, target selection and repeated cutting versus hex-bit insertion, setscrew torque, collar adjustment and response tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: All shoots must be severed near target height, no flower cut, and shears returned closed; candidate passes on locked adjustment and two safe axial stops.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate an articulated mechanism with safety constraints, but cutting selective targets is materially different from tuning and validating a shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Hold a spring-return safety loop released while operating a bottle-opening rocker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sustained bimanual contact against a torsion spring while pressing a separate control; no tool insertion, collar adjustment, or relocking.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle opens while the loop remains released; releasing the loop prevents success. Numeric loop/rocker details are only partly reported in the record.
comparisons.reason: The candidate commissions damping through captive-screw tool access, collar tuning, and measured impact cycles; this record tests simultaneous spring restraint and bottle actuation.

comparisons.objective: Reorient two eggs small-end-down and place them in carton cups.
comparisons.physical_skill: Shape-based orientation, delicate grasping, rotation, and placement into tapered supports.
comparisons.success_condition: Both eggs are centered, seated, within 20 degrees of small-end-down, at rest, and released for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Delicate object reorientation and packing does not test adjustment locking, recessed-tool reacquisition, or dynamic damping performance.

comparisons.objective: Loosen two bottle caps before loading their basket into an autoclave.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rotate two exposed caps, then push a basket into a chamber.
comparisons.success_condition: Both caps reach at least 60 degrees loose before the basket enters; inserting a tightly capped bottle latches failure.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve rotation and safe sequencing, this record has no fine recessed tool, moving socket, relocking, or iterative response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Pass a parcel through a self-closing gate onto a conveyor without gate contact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-loaded gate open with one hand while pushing a parcel through with the other, then release it gently.
comparisons.success_condition: Parcel reaches the run-off plate through the gateway, remains on the table and upright, gate closes, and arms retreat; gate contact invalidates the run.
comparisons.reason: It tests sustained bimanual gate restraint and transport, not damper setting, fastener access, or measured stopping behavior.

comparisons.objective: Peel a sterile pouch and transfer its instrument to a sterile drape without contamination.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual peeling against a seal, controlled dropping, sterile-clearance management, and waste placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Pouch is peeled, forceps land on the drape, contamination never occurs, sheets enter bins, and arms retreat.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual peeling and contamination control are materially different from fine hex engagement, collar tuning, locking, and dynamic impact validation.

comparisons.objective: Balance and lock a counterweighted service arm at an intermediate level position.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support a loaded pivot, translate a counterweight, align and insert a free pin, then release.
comparisons.success_condition: The mass is retained and the arm remains passively level after both hands withdraw; the record body does not state its numeric equilibrium tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Both adjust and lock a mechanism, but this record tests gravitational balancing plus through-hole pin insertion; the candidate tests captive setscrew access and iterative hydraulic stopping response.

comparisons.objective: Lower a gas-spring overbed table to a marked height and leave its column locked.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a release paddle while pressing a spring-loaded top, then sequence release to avoid rebound.
comparisons.success_condition: Height error is within 10 mm for principal credit, column remains locked within 3 mm for 2 seconds, and excessive rebound, tilt, or shin force invalidates the run.
comparisons.reason: This is force-coordinated height positioning through a held release. It does not adjust a damping parameter with a recessed tool or evaluate repeated impact-energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Flatten a spring-creased open carton for recycling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply a steep, sustained pushing trajectory through a folding arc until the creases set.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton shear reaches at least 80 degrees, lies below 2.5 cm, is still and released; partial folding or spring-back fails.
comparisons.reason: Crease collapse and flattening do not exercise tool alignment, lock preservation, tuning, or controlled axial stopping.

comparisons.objective: Refit a delta robot's sprung parallel-rod pair onto four ball studs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually lift and spread a spring-coupled pair, align four sockets, and clip them onto studs without overstretching.
comparisons.success_condition: All four cups seat within 2.5 mm, the pair is released and still for 1 second, with no drop or spread to 92 mm.
comparisons.reason: This tests compliant multi-point alignment and snap fitting, not damper commissioning or iterative dynamic-response adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Move a live-wire surrogate off a walkway using an insulated stick.
comparisons.physical_skill: Indirect manipulation of an articulated cable with a rigid tool while maintaining electrical-clearance constraints.
comparisons.success_condition: No robot link touches the cable; the cable clears the walkway, its plug enters the parking zone, and it remains on the table.
comparisons.reason: Indirect cable pushing and hazard avoidance share only generic tool use with the candidate and lack fastening, tuning, or damping tests.

comparisons.objective: Load a corded blender into a service lift and start it without trapping the cord or an arm.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate a rigid appliance and articulated cord, clear a moving door, and press a control.
comparisons.success_condition: Blender and entire cord are behind the safety line when the button is pressed; entrapment or lift failure scores zero.
comparisons.reason: The common final control press is generic. This record primarily tests cable routing and door clearance, not adjustment locking or repeatable impact stops.

comparisons.objective: Build a stable 3-2-1 pyramid from six cans.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated precise placement and bridging on progressively less stable supports.
comparisons.success_condition: Six upright, resting cans form the specified three tiers; tipping or single-can tower shortcuts invalidate credit.
comparisons.reason: Stable stacking tests placement and support geometry, with no mechanism adjustment, tool reacquisition, or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Unload a soup tray from a pass shelf and serve its bowl without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tray extraction and leveling followed by careful bowl transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Tray lies flat, bowl reaches the placemat, and no more than 10 ml-equivalent spills; severe tipping fails.
comparisons.reason: Load stabilization and spill avoidance are meaningfully different from fine fastener/collar manipulation and measured damper response.

comparisons.objective: Clamp two aligned stacked boards with a one-hand bar clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Position opposing jaws around a stack, drive a sliding ratchet jaw, establish force, and release the clamp.
comparisons.success_condition: Pads have at most 0.5 mm gaps, clamping force is at least 20 N, alignment and placement tolerances hold, and the released assembly stays still for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: It shares locking and force verification only generically; it tests external jaw placement and clamping, not recessed hex access, moving-socket reacquisition, or damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Measure and mark 300 mm on a board with a spring-return tape.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a tape extended against spring return while the other hand places a precise pen mark.
comparisons.success_condition: A single released-pen mark is within 4 mm of 300 mm while the tape was extended beyond it; success holds for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: This tests sustained bimanual measurement and marking, not setting retention or dynamic impact tuning.

comparisons.objective: Fit a 1U blanking panel at U6 in a server rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify rack-unit holes, align two distant clips, insert and seat both ends, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel edges are within 3 mm of U6, both ends are home, and the robot remains clear for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Dual-ended panel alignment and insertion are materially different from captive-screw/collar adjustment and repeated stopping tests.

comparisons.objective: Hang a washed bottle mouth-down on a drying-rack peg.
comparisons.physical_skill: Invert a hollow object, align its mouth over a peg, lower it, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Peg penetrates at least 3 cm, bottle is within 30 degrees of vertical and hangs clear, still and released for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Peg insertion and hanging do not test tool torque, lock reacquisition, adjustment, or dynamic response.

comparisons.objective: Remove vitamins and seasonings from a dementia patient's table without disturbing the meal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and transfer three rigid objects into a box while avoiding protected objects.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle and both shakers are in the box; moving, tilting, or lifting the plate or mug invalidates the score. No separate spec versions or tighter release thresholds are provided.
comparisons.reason: Semantic selection and pick-and-place avoidance are unrelated to mechanical commissioning beyond generic grasping.

comparisons.objective: Power on a bench supply and set its voltage knob from 12 V to 9 V.
comparisons.physical_skill: Press a latching button, grasp and rotate an exposed knob precisely, release it, and avoid disturbing adjacent controls.
comparisons.success_condition: Supply is on, voltage is within 0.2 V of 9 V, other knobs remain within 3 degrees, unit stays in place, and arms retreat for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest exposed-control task, but it lacks recessed hex insertion, captive-screw loosening/relocking, moving-socket reacquisition, and iterative physical-response testing under energy and force limits.

comparisons.objective: Crack a walnut in a hand nutcracker and sort kernel from shell.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually compress sprung handles with force, then manipulate and sort small fragments.
comparisons.success_condition: Both jaws apply at least 40 N for 0.1 seconds, kernel enters the bowl, all shell enters the saucer, and arms retreat.
comparisons.reason: Forceful fracture and fragment sorting do not test parameter adjustment, fastener locking, or repeatable axial stopping.

comparisons.objective: Locate a DC earth fault by sectionalizing fuse circuits one at a time.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeatedly extract and reinsert fuse carriers while reading a meter and preserving circuit availability.
comparisons.success_condition: Only the faulty F3 feeder remains open, with no episode of two circuits open together; the record supplies geometric carrier criteria but no separate spec versions.
comparisons.reason: It tests diagnostic search and fuse extraction/reinsertion. The candidate instead tunes a mechanical response and explicitly does not extract its captive screw.

comparisons.objective: Grind peppercorns while holding a mortar stationary.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually stabilize a vessel and execute repeated circular pestle contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Five rounds-equivalent of valid rubbing occur with minimal mortar motion, then the pestle is returned upright and arms retreat.
comparisons.reason: Sustained circular rubbing and stabilization do not exercise recessed fastening, collar locking, or impact-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Install a pressure-relief wheelchair cushion in the correct orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Recognize orientation, rotate a bulky cushion through regrasping, and lower it between guards.
comparisons.success_condition: Cushion is correctly oriented, flat, centered, near the backrest and still; wrong orientation earns zero. No separate spec versions are available.
comparisons.reason: Bulky-object reorientation and placement are materially different from precision tool access and dynamic damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Fit elbows to copper and plastic pipes, inserting a support sleeve only in the plastic pipe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Perform three ordered coaxial push insertions selected by pipe material.
comparisons.success_condition: Both elbows are seated and the plastic joint contains its insert; inserting into copper or first seating plastic without its insert causes failure. No separate spec versions are available.
comparisons.reason: Ordered push-fit insertion is a different tested ability from captive fastener manipulation, rotary tuning, and impact validation.

comparisons.objective: Remove one tissue from a pop-up box while leaving the next tissue presented.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pinch and manipulate coupled deformable sheets without tipping the box or extracting both.
comparisons.success_condition: First tissue reaches the tray, second protrudes at least 10 mm while remaining partly inside, box returns to its pose, and grippers clear for 1 second.
comparisons.reason: Deformable-sheet separation and presentation are unrelated to rigid damper commissioning and its tool/force-control sequence.

comparisons.objective: Cut a DIN rail to a measured 250 mm length using a manual or powered cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Position and hold a long rail, then operate a lever; later version adds toggle clamping and button actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: First cut within 1 mm, with under 0.5 mm rail motion; partial credit at 5 mm or for pre-cut alignment.
comparisons.reason: The candidate commissions a damper by unlocking, finely adjusting, relocking, and iteratively evaluating physical stopping response. Rail measurement, clamping, and one-shot cutting test a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Hang two fragile baubles by threading their attached hooks over stand branches.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp small caps, control swinging loads, guide open hooks over 5 mm rods, and release without dropping.
comparisons.success_condition: Both baubles hang motionless for 2 seconds; any breakage proxy zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: Hook placement and fragile-load control do not test captive-screw tool use, collar setting retention, or iterative dynamic damping calibration.

comparisons.objective: Separate a toy ladybird from crumbs, putting the crumbs in a bin and the ladybird in a garden pot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object classification and selective pick-and-place among small mixed items.
comparisons.success_condition: Correctly sorted crumbs and ladybird without misplacing the protected object.
comparisons.reason: Selective sorting is meaningfully different from tool-mediated adjustment, locking, and repeated force/energy-response testing.

comparisons.objective: Place the last cake slice on plate 1 rather than the nearest plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Read or infer the numbered target and perform a simple pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Cake rests on the plate associated with ticket 1; any other destination scores zero.
comparisons.reason: This primarily tests visual-semantic target selection and placement, not contact-rich adjustment or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Dispense exactly ten pre-counted tablets from a tray trough into a held vial while leaving six others behind.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a vial aloft and tip a granular tray without spilling or mixing tablets.
comparisons.success_condition: All ten counted tablets enter the raised vial, all six others remain in the counting area, and none spill.
comparisons.reason: Granular pouring and count preservation test a different mechanism and outcome from damper unlocking, fine rotary adjustment, relocking, and stopping-response validation.

comparisons.objective: Place a drain pan before removing an engine drain plug, then retain the plug in a parts dish.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequence pan placement and plug extraction while avoiding a represented spill.
comparisons.success_condition: Pan remains under the outlet whenever the plug is out; full credit also requires the plug in the dish.
comparisons.reason: Although both enforce safe sequencing, this record tests containment-before-extraction, not fine tool engagement, setting retention, or iterative dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Prepare a soup place setting for a person with dementia by leaving only the needed large-handled spoon.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic selection plus removal and placement of utensils.
comparisons.success_condition: Spoon lies properly on the mat and both forks lie properly off it.
comparisons.reason: Utensil selection and pick-and-place are unrelated to mechanical commissioning. The record lacks a separate task spec, but its body supplies sufficient scoring detail to establish distinction.

comparisons.objective: Vent the warm cryostat, wait, remove its sample, and leave the cold cryostat untouched.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify status lights, press the correct control, wait, remove a lid and sample, and place the sample.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct warm-side sequence with a three-second wait and sample in tray; touching or venting the cold unit or premature lid motion zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: This tests equipment selection and timed safety sequencing, not rotary adjustment with a moving lock socket or measured energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Gently place a stir bar into a tilted round-bottom flask and return the flask upright to its ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold and tilt fragile glassware while guiding a small bar into its neck without a damaging impact.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar remains inside, flask returns upright and released in its ring, and impact/drop/tip thresholds are never violated.
comparisons.reason: Fragile-vessel support and gentle insertion are different from damper setting adjustment and repeated stopping tests.

comparisons.objective: Refit a long wardrobe rail between one closed and one open support.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually tilt a long part, insert one end, swing the other end down, level, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Both ends are supported, the rail is within 1 degree of level, still, and released.
comparisons.reason: Long-part tilt-in insertion does not test fine hex-tool manipulation, captive locking, setting preservation, or dynamic response optimization.

comparisons.objective: Measure voltage by simultaneously seating two probes in named L and N terminal openings.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually grasp and precisely insert two fine probe tips while avoiding neighboring openings.
comparisons.success_condition: Both held tips reach the correct clamps/openings continuously for one second; entering another terminal zeros the trial.
comparisons.reason: It shares fine tool alignment and insertion, but the tested ability is simultaneous electrical-probe placement. It has no unlock-adjust-relock sequence or iterative mechanical response criterion.

comparisons.objective: Drop a glove box safely, remove its old filter, and insert a replacement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Simultaneously squeeze two sprung walls, articulate the box, extract a tabbed filter, and align and insert a new filter.
comparisons.success_condition: No stop is forced; old filter is out, new filter is seated within tight pose tolerances, and everything is released and still.
comparisons.reason: This tests simultaneous compliant release and component replacement, not adjustment retention and energy-dissipation commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Release a screwdriver from a spring clamp and finish holding it over a marker.
comparisons.physical_skill: Operate a spring clamp, extract the tool, and establish verified opposing fingertip contacts.
comparisons.success_condition: Tool is safely freed and held by the left gripper over the target without dropping it or moving the base.
comparisons.reason: Clamp release and extraction differ from loosening a captive setscrew, relocating and reacquiring its socket, tuning a collar, and validating stopping behavior. The body gives no separate numeric objective/skill rubric beyond its contact-based completion description.

comparisons.objective: Add a block to a shared tower while another robot arm is also building it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Time a pick-and-place around another moving arm and avoid robot-robot contact.
comparisons.success_condition: Green block rests on the tower; any arm contact zeros the run.
comparisons.reason: Shared-workspace turn-taking and stacking are unrelated to damper commissioning mechanics and force/energy outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Use two sticks together as tongs to retrieve an out-of-reach cup and stand it on a stone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually wield two independent tools, maintain opposing contact, lift, carry, and place a cup.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup stands upright on the target stone for two seconds; partial credit if merely removed from the pit.
comparisons.reason: Improvised bimanual tong manipulation tests coordinated transport, not fine adjustment, locking, or dynamic response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Move four cubes into a box while stopping both arms whenever a person raises a stop paddle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Monitor an external signal, interrupt two-arm motion, resume, and complete pick-and-place.
comparisons.success_condition: Combined gripper motion stays within 3 cm while the paddle is raised; credit then depends on cubes boxed.
comparisons.reason: It tests human-signaled interruptibility and resumption rather than mechanical setting adjustment or commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Remove one terminal block from a loose DIN rail without disturbing adjacent blocks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the rail while pushing, tipping, and sliding a snap-fit block off its latch.
comparisons.success_condition: Target block is released into the tray while neighbors and rail remain within strict displacement limits.
comparisons.reason: Contact-rich latch release and dismounting are different from reversible captive-screw unlocking, fine collar rotation, relocking, and repeated damping tests.

comparisons.objective: Knock a spent espresso puck from a portafilter into a knock box and return the portafilter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grip, invert, and sharply impact a held container to break a bond without dropping or digging.
comparisons.success_condition: Puck lands in the box and the released portafilter returns stably to its holder; unsafe release methods zero the run.
comparisons.reason: Impact-induced ejection tests momentum generation. The candidate instead adjusts a dissipative mechanism and evaluates controlled stopping without bottoming or overload.

comparisons.objective: Capture the distributed spring preload of a twelve-cell pack using a cross-key.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress a loose pressure plate with one arm while inserting a separate retaining key with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: All twelve contacts and retained preload remain correct after both grippers withdraw.
comparisons.reason: Both involve retaining a mechanical setting, but this record tests simultaneous distributed compression and key insertion. It does not test fine rotary tool work or iterative dynamic-response tuning. The record body does not expose separate numeric scoring tiers.

comparisons.objective: Align a loose splash-shield panel with a body hole and fasten both layers using a push-in clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold two holes aligned while inserting and seating a sprung retainer.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel is flat and aligned within 1.5 mm, clip is upright and fully home, and the assembly remains still.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual hole alignment and push-fastening test assembly insertion, not adjustable-damper unlocking, setting selection, relocking, or dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Identify and fully reseat the one half-inserted network plug without disturbing three seated neighbors.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual fault finding and constrained plug insertion among adjacent cables.
comparisons.success_condition: Loose plug reaches at least 22 mm depth, all neighbors remain seated, and the robot releases all plugs.
comparisons.reason: Connector fault correction is explicitly a plug-insertion family and lacks the candidate's fine adjustment, lock retention, and stopping-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Unload three fruits from a shared bin while another robot arm works in the same space.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick and place around an independently moving coworker while avoiding collision.
comparisons.success_condition: Credit per fruit resting in the tray; any robot-robot contact zeros the run.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic collision avoidance during transport tests a different ability from localized tool use and damper calibration.

comparisons.objective: Unplug a spot welder's USB-C cable, put the plug down, and place the welder in its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually stabilize a device, pull a close-fit plug straight out, then regrasp and orient the device into a pocket.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug is hand-extracted and released, welder is seated correctly, both arms retreat, and nothing is dropped or opened.
comparisons.reason: This is connector extraction and device placement, not mechanical adjustment and iterative dynamic commissioning. The body supplies scoring but no separate task-spec version.

comparisons.objective: Remove a push-and-turn child-resistant bottle cap.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a free bottle while simultaneously pressing and rotating the cap, then lift it off.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap is off after sufficient pressed anticlockwise rotation, with no spill or bottle tip; loose cap earns partial credit.
