comparisons.reason: It shares bounded rotation and a lock condition, but tests coupled push-and-turn removal. The candidate requires separate hex unlocking, bit withdrawal, collar tuning, moving-socket reacquisition, relocking, and measured dynamic trials.

comparisons.objective: Hold an SO-101 shoulder bracket aloft while inserting a servo into its close-fit pocket in the correct orientation.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually support a loose part, orient a servo, perform close-clearance insertion, press it home, and set the assembly down.
comparisons.success_condition: Servo is correctly oriented, aligned, and fully seated; bracket is upright and released, with both arms retracted.
comparisons.reason: Close-fit robot assembly insertion is meaningfully different from adjustment-and-test commissioning. The body provides explicit step thresholds but no separate task-spec version.

comparisons.objective: Restock a spring-loaded shelf lane while preserving stock order; candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber through repeated impact tests.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR holds a resisting pusher while placing cartons. Candidate performs fine hex-bit engagement, captive-screw torque, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires four ordered cartons and a released pusher at 9.2–11.0 cm. Candidate requires two safe ≥0.85 J axial stops within travel, velocity, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: The tested abilities and physical outcomes differ meaningfully: bimanual resisted loading versus precision adjustment followed by dynamic damping validation.

comparisons.objective: Fold sprung carton flaps in the required order; candidate tunes and locks an industrial damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR holds spring-returning flaps while folding covering flaps. Candidate uses a fine hex tool and collar, then operates a separate test control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires all four flaps closed in order and still for 1 s. Candidate requires two consecutive safe stopping cycles plus retained adjustment. PR lacks a separate task specification, but its body states the decisive rubric.
comparisons.reason: Shared spring resistance and sequencing are generic; flap containment does not test tool reacquisition, locking, or measured impact response.

comparisons.objective: Remove a fragile jar lid before separately moving jar and lid; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR grasps and transports separable ceramic parts. Candidate aligns a 1.5 mm bit, applies bounded torque, rotates a small collar, reacquires the moved socket, and cycles a fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: PR forbids moving the jar with its lid attached and rewards safe placement on a padded tray. Candidate scores force-, travel-, rebound-, and drift-bounded repeated stops. No separate spec is available for PR.
comparisons.reason: Safe fragile-object separation and transport tests a different ability from mechanical adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Place a non-slip mat beneath a heavy bowl without spilling; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR tips and steadies a 1.2 kg bowl while inserting a mat underneath. Candidate performs recessed-tool access, collar adjustment, relocking, and guarded test actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR limits bowl tilt to 30° and foot motion to 4 cm, then requires a level bowl on the mat. Candidate requires repeated non-bottoming impacts within energy, force, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual support-and-underlay insertion does not test fine fastener access or closed-loop dynamic damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Select and insert a PH2 bit into a screwdriver holder; candidate uses a hex bit to unlock, adjust, and relock a damper before testing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both involve fine bit alignment, but PR performs one 0.05 mm-clearance hex-shank insertion while steadying a tool. Candidate must engage a recessed socket, torque a captive screw, withdraw, rotate the collar, reacquire the relocated socket, and tighten.
comparisons.success_condition: PR succeeds with the PH2 bit seated ≥9 mm within tight pose tolerances and both arms retracted. Candidate additionally requires retained setting and two force/travel-safe dynamic cycles.
comparisons.reason: There is primitive-level overlap in hexagonal alignment, but the candidate meaningfully extends it into captive fastener manipulation, moving-socket reacquisition, locking, and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Synchronize a generator to grid phase and speed before closing its breaker; candidate mechanically adjusts a damper from impact response.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR reads an instrument and taps panel buttons at the correct time. Candidate physically manipulates a fine tool and collar, clears the mechanism, and actuates a guarded test control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires matched pointer speed and breaker closure within a phase window; its rubric gives no full geometry spec. Candidate requires two repeatable axial stops under explicit energy, travel, velocity, force, rebound, and drift bounds.
comparisons.reason: Both include iterative control decisions, but generator phase timing does not test mechanical unlocking, precision adjustment, relocking, or energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Insert the final motor magnet while preventing an adjacent loose magnet from jumping out; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR holds one magnet down while aligning and inserting another against modeled magnetic forces. Candidate uses a hex bit and rotating collar, then runs a physical impact fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the correct magnet flush, adjacent magnet displacement ≤6 mm, and arms returned. Candidate requires locked retention and two safe stopping cycles.
comparisons.reason: Force-coupled bimanual insertion is materially different from fastener/collar manipulation and measured damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Twist an ice tray to release cubes, tip them into a dish, and replace the tray; candidate tunes a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR applies opposing bimanual torques and pours multiple loose objects. Candidate performs small-socket tool use, fine collar rotation, relocking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires a qualifying 12° twist, all eight cubes in the dish, and tray replacement. Candidate requires two bounded dynamic stops with no damage or setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Opposing-torque flexing and pouring do not test precision fastener access or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Heat and scrape three paint patches without damaging glass; candidate adjusts and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR coordinates a heat gun and scraper continuously with two hands. Candidate sequences hex-tool torque, bit withdrawal, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and test actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires ≥80% of each patch removed, tools returned, and no glass heating failure. Candidate requires repeated safe energy absorption and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual thermal process/tool-path control is a different tested ability from mechanical adjustment and impact-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Build two scaffold footings in the safe board–plate–tube order; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR places and aligns large support components and inserts tubes into collars. Candidate manipulates a recessed fine fastener and small collar before cycling a fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires correctly stacked, upright tubes and latches sinking failures. Candidate requires force-, travel-, rebound-, and drift-bounded impacts. PR has no separate spec beyond its detailed body.
comparisons.reason: Ordered structural placement and tube insertion are not equivalent to precision adjustment, locking, and dynamic performance validation.

comparisons.objective: Open a piano lid while installing its support prop; candidate tunes and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR continuously supports a loaded lid with one arm while the other swings and seats a prop. Candidate uses a fine hex tool and collar, then performs hands-clear test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the lid resting on its prop without a drop. Candidate requires two safe repeatable axial stops and ≤2° collar drift. PR lacks a separate spec.
comparisons.reason: Support transfer and prop insertion test different mechanics and outcomes from damper adjustment and commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Place an emergency call through a locked phone’s safe UI route; candidate commissions a mechanical damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR performs precise touchscreen swipes and taps while avoiding passcode entry. Candidate performs contact-rich tool alignment, torque, collar manipulation, and fixture actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires a clean 911 call maintained for 3 s; any passcode attempt fails. Candidate requires two bounded physical stopping cycles without damage or drift. PR has no separate spec.
comparisons.reason: Touchscreen procedural interaction is unrelated to mechanical adjustment and force-controlled dynamic testing.

comparisons.objective: Mix flour and liquid into dough while steadying a loose bowl; candidate adjusts and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR coordinates sustained spoon motion with bowl stabilization amid granular contents. Candidate performs fine fastener/collar work followed by guarded impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires ≥95% of flour mixed with spill and tip limits. Candidate requires repeated non-bottoming stops under energy, velocity, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Continuous mixing and stabilization test a different physical capability from precision locking and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Identify empty opaque bottles by weight and recycle only those; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR lifts objects to infer hidden mass, then sorts them. Candidate aligns and torques a fine tool, rotates and locks a collar, and evaluates impact behavior.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both empty bottles upright in the bin, with no full bottle discarded or bottle tipped. Candidate requires two safe stopping cycles and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Haptic mass discrimination and sorting are materially unrelated to mechanical adjustment and damping validation.

comparisons.objective: Fill a fuel can only after placing it safely on the ground, then return it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR transports a can and positions a fuel nozzle while observing a grounding rule. Candidate performs recessed-tool manipulation, collar adjustment, locking, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR permanently fails if fuel flows while the can is not safely grounded; full credit follows filling and return. Candidate fails unsafe energized adjustment and requires two bounded impacts. PR lacks a separate spec.
comparisons.reason: The shared safe sequencing is generic; fuel-container handling does not test damper adjustment or dynamic stopping behavior.

comparisons.objective: Press a spring-raised picture-frame back flush and lock it with four rotating clips; candidate unlocks, adjusts, and relocks a damper collar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both include rotation and locking, but PR holds a large sprung board down while turning four exposed clips and swapping hands. Candidate engages a recessed 1.5 mm socket, applies bounded screw torque, withdraws the bit, finely turns an 11.2 mm collar, and reacquires the relocated socket.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires four clips rotated ≥80°, back flush within 3 mm/1.5°, hands clear, and 1 s stability. Candidate requires lock retention plus two safe dynamic impact cycles.
comparisons.reason: There is locking-level overlap, but the mechanisms and tested outcomes differ: spring-back containment versus fine captive-fastener access and response-based damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a 2×2 battery pack by placing holder halves and inserting four correctly oriented cells; candidate tunes and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR performs repeated tight peg-in-cup insertions and fixture alignment. Candidate performs fine hex engagement, torque, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires all cells seated positive-up, top holder aligned within 2 mm, and the assembly still. Candidate requires two force/travel-safe stops and no lock drift.
comparisons.reason: Precision assembly insertion is not the same tested ability as adjustable damping setup and dynamic validation.

comparisons.objective: Open a stepladder fully and engage its spreader lock; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR steadies one ladder section while pulling the other against a closing spring until a latch seats. Candidate manipulates a fine screw and collar, then cycles a test carriage.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires full opening, spreader engagement, four feet down, and no fall. Candidate requires two bounded energy-absorption cycles and retained adjustment. PR has no separate spec.
comparisons.reason: Large articulated deployment and latching differ from precision tool use and measured damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Crossfade two radio channels without dead air or excessive overlap; candidate mechanically tunes a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR moves two long-throw faders in coordinated opposite directions. Candidate uses a hex bit and collar, clears the fixture, and actuates a separate guarded control.
comparisons.success_condition: PR enforces trajectory constraints and final fader positions held for 1 s. Candidate enforces mechanical lock retention and two physical stopping cycles under force and travel limits. PR lacks a separate spec.
comparisons.reason: Both require coordinated adjustment, but audio fader trajectory control does not test tool access, locking, impact contact, or energy absorption.

comparisons.objective: Exchange obstructed enclosure modules and close the enclosure; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR removes, collects, aligns, and installs multiple rail-guided modules around an obstruction. Candidate performs fine captive-fastener and collar manipulation followed by dynamic testing.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires correct replacement identities, seating, collection, lid retention, clearance, and stability; exact numeric thresholds are absent from the available body. Candidate requires two bounded stopping cycles and no drift or damage.
comparisons.reason: Module exchange and enclosure closeout test multi-part extraction/insertion, not adjustment of damping response.

comparisons.objective: Insert both ends of a short patch cord into two tester jacks without unseating the first; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR coordinates deformable-cord slack and two connector insertions. Candidate performs rigid fine-tool alignment, screw torque, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded impact cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires both plugs inserted ≥15 mm, tester units unmoved, and grippers released. Candidate requires two safe axial stops and lock retention.
comparisons.reason: Connector insertion with cord management is a different tested ability from mechanical adjustment and dynamic stopping validation.

comparisons.objective: Clear only the cartons obstructing a photo-eye beam; candidate adjusts and tests a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR uses spatial reasoning to move selected cartons minimally while keeping them upright. Candidate performs fine tool/collar manipulation and fixture control actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the beam clear, blockers moved ≤10 cm, non-blockers untouched, and all cartons upright and still. Candidate requires two bounded impact cycles without bottoming, overload, rebound, or drift.
comparisons.reason: Selective obstacle relocation is unrelated to damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a flashlight cap, pour out its battery, and safely set parts down; candidate loosens a captive setscrew, adjusts a collar, and retightens it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Both use rotational manipulation, but PR performs two large cap regrasp twists, complete threaded separation, pouring, and placement. Candidate keeps the screw captive, withdraws/re-engages a 1.5 mm bit, preserves collar setting during bounded tightening, and tests impacts.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires cap separation, battery in a box, and safe final placement. Candidate requires retained adjustment and two safe force/travel-bounded cycles.
comparisons.reason: Rotational primitive overlap does not erase the meaningful difference between threaded disassembly/pouring and precision locking plus dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Extract a retaining pin while supporting a weighted carriage; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR coordinates load support and fastener extraction to prevent a drop. Candidate uses a recessed hex tool and adjustment collar, then operates an impact fixture.
comparisons.success_condition: PR reports safe pin extraction and retained carriage height, but its available body omits exact scoring thresholds. Candidate requires two explicit energy-, velocity-, travel-, force-, rebound-, and drift-bounded stops.
comparisons.reason: Load-bearing support transfer during extraction is materially different from fine adjustment and repeated damping validation.

comparisons.objective: Hold a spring-loaded release collet while pulling a pipe from a push-fit fitting; candidate unlocks and adjusts a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: PR maintains collet depression with one hand while extracting and placing a pipe with the other. Candidate sequences hex-bit engagement, screw loosening, bit withdrawal, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, retightening, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: PR requires the pipe extracted and laid flat, with staged credit for collet depression and pull distance. Candidate requires two safe stopping cycles and ≤2° setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve releasing a lock before manipulation, simultaneous collet-hold-and-pull tests a different mechanism and outcome from captive-screw adjustment and response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Stabilize a loaf and saw off a safe, thickness-controlled slice.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual claw holding and repeated knife sawing; no fine socket work, locking collar, or dynamic commissioning.
comparisons.success_condition: A 1–2 cm slice is fully severed while both grippers remain at least 3 cm from the blade.
comparisons.reason: Food cutting tests bimanual stabilization and sawing, not lock-adjust-relock manipulation followed by measured impact tuning.

comparisons.objective: Open, latch, release, and lift a stick umbrella.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a handle while pushing a spring-loaded runner linearly until it latches.
comparisons.success_condition: Runner latched after 95% of 12 cm travel, released, and umbrella lifted by its handle.
comparisons.reason: Its spring-loaded linear latch does not require tool insertion, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, torque-bounded locking, or iterative response adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Form, tighten, and release an overhand knot in a cord.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable loop formation, threading, bimanual tensioning, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: Released knot remains intact five seconds and, for full credit, previously passes the 117 cm suspended-span check.
comparisons.reason: Deformable knot tying tests topology and tension management, unlike rigid damper adjustment and dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Manually close a powered valve actuator after power loss by engaging its override clutch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a declutch lever while turning a handwheel until a clutch dog engages, then continue turning.
comparisons.success_condition: Clutch engaged and valve within 5 degrees of its closed stop for three seconds.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve a stateful mechanism and rotation, this tests bimanual clutch engagement and valve closure, not fine tool-mediated unlock-adjust-relock work or tuning from impact response.

comparisons.objective: Empty a robot-vacuum dustbin without spilling, then reinstall it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Lift and position a bin, hold a release button, manage falling particles, and reseat the bin.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 9 of 10 dust balls enter the waste box, the bin is seated within stated pose tolerances with doors shut, and arms return.
comparisons.reason: Granular transfer and reseating are meaningfully different from fine locking hardware manipulation and damper performance commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Water soil while keeping a sprung leaf aside and avoiding wet leaves.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hold-aside and controlled pouring of discrete liquid proxies.
comparisons.success_condition: Latest versions require at least 90 ml on soil, at most 10 ml on leaves, restored leaf and jug, release, and arm return.
comparisons.reason: This tests pouring and obstacle displacement, not precision socket engagement, collar locking, or iterative dynamic tuning.

comparisons.objective: Open a folding fan fully while keeping one guard stick fixed.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and sweeping a second stick around a stiff pivot.
comparisons.success_condition: Fan spread at least 135 degrees, lying on its stand, with arms returned for full credit.
comparisons.reason: Arc motion around a pivot shares generic rotation only; it lacks tool use, a moving lock socket, bounded tightening, and response-based adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Intercept two designated moving slot cars while a third keeps racing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual interception of moving objects, guide extraction, transport, and matched placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Yellow and blue are extracted while moving and placed on matching pads; red continues, forbidden contact is avoided, and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Dynamic interception and sorting test moving-object capture, not adjustment and commissioning of a fixed mechanical damper.

comparisons.objective: Square a racked glued face frame by equalizing its diagonals.
comparisons.physical_skill: Apply opposed forces to shear a compliant four-bar frame without lifting, sliding out, or breaking joints.
comparisons.success_condition: Diagonal difference at most 2 mm, frame inside its outline, grippers clear, and motion under 1 mm for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests bimanual geometric correction of a compliant assembly, not fine lock manipulation or iterative impact-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Relink a 230/400 V motor from delta to the correct star configuration for 400 V.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove, align, and seat small conductive links over specified terminal-stud pairs; store the spare link.
comparisons.success_condition: Two links form the winding-end star bridge and the third is in the lid; shorts, delta remnants, or loose links fail.
comparisons.reason: Electrical-terminal configuration requires multi-part insertion and rule selection, but not a captive screw, rotating adjustment collar, or physical response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Seal a filled carton with a hand tape gun.
comparisons.physical_skill: Track a tool along a seam under pressure, tear tape, and smooth hanging tabs.
comparisons.success_condition: Tape covers the 160 mm seam within 10 mm, is torn, tabs extend at least 24 mm down both ends, flaps are flat, and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Continuous tape-tool tracking and adhesion proxy control differ from fine rotational adjustment, locking, and repeated impact evaluation.

comparisons.objective: Peel a cucumber while preserving both ends.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual holding/reorientation and force-bounded surface following with a swivel peeler.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 44 of 48 middle patches peeled, none gouged, ends untouched, no blade-hand contact or fall, then release and stillness.
comparisons.reason: Both demand bounded force and tool alignment, but peeling tests repeated curved-surface cutting rather than socket engagement and dynamic damper tuning.

comparisons.objective: Transfer a spring clothes peg and clip a photo corner to a thin wire.
comparisons.physical_skill: Squeeze and retain a spring clip, align its jaws around a 1.2 mm wire and 0.3 mm photo, then release.
comparisons.success_condition: Second peg holds the near corner on the wire for two seconds, photo remains hung, and grippers are over 4 cm away.
comparisons.reason: Fine alignment and squeeze-release are shared generic primitives, but the tested mechanism and outcome differ from torque locking and response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Trace the leaking coolant branch and shut only its associated valve.
comparisons.physical_skill: Visual pipe tracing across crossings and quarter-turn lever actuation without disturbing other valves.
comparisons.success_condition: Spraying valve at least 70 degrees shut, other valves under 20 degrees, hands clear for one second; wrong-valve motion past 45 degrees fails.
comparisons.reason: It tests causal line tracing and selective isolation, not fine tool insertion, mechanical setting retention, or iterative impact calibration.

comparisons.objective: Register an aluminium workpiece accurately against an L-shaped corner stop.
comparisons.physical_skill: Cross-workspace handoff, planar placement, squaring, and contact registration against two faces.
comparisons.success_condition: Block flat, all gaps at most 1 mm, sides within 2 degrees of square, and still for one second.
comparisons.reason: Precision placement against datum faces is different from manipulating and locking a damper setting and validating its dynamic behavior.

comparisons.objective: Identify the higher-friction sled using a fair controlled test.
comparisons.physical_skill: Equalize masses, load launchers, operate a button, observe travel, and place the inferred sled.
comparisons.success_condition: Both sleds launch at equal total mass without hitting the wall, shorter travel identifies higher friction, and only that sled is on the red mat.
comparisons.reason: This is experimental design and comparative inference; it lacks the candidate's fine lock-adjust-relock sequence and direct iterative tuning of a component.

comparisons.objective: Move five fragile upright tiles into a box in as few trips as possible.
comparisons.physical_skill: Batch grasping and transporting multiple thin upright objects without tipping or dropping.
comparisons.success_condition: All tiles stand inside the box with no tip, fall, or drop; score depends on trip count.
comparisons.reason: Fragile multi-object transport tests batch grasp stability and risk management, not mechanical adjustment or commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve an occluded charger by its cord without moving the obstructing box.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate an articulated cord, manage tension and wedge geometry, hand off, and place the charger.
comparisons.success_condition: Charger rests inside the tray, box remains within 2 cm and 10 degrees, and grippers clear the cord and charger.
comparisons.reason: Occluded deformable retrieval and tension management are unrelated to rigid fine-tool locking and impact-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Aim a loaded inspection arm to +15 degrees and lock it there.
comparisons.physical_skill: One gripper supports a loaded articulated arm while the other tightens an indexed clamp; then both withdraw.
comparisons.success_condition: Arm retains the set elevation for two seconds after release; locking before aiming fails.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest adjustment-and-lock task, but it tests simultaneous support and clamp tightening at a prescribed angle. The candidate adds recessed-bit insertion, captive-screw loosening, bit withdrawal, collar rotation, moved-socket reacquisition, guarded cycling, and iterative response-based setting. The record lacks a full spec, but its stated mechanism and outcome still establish a meaningful distinction.

comparisons.objective: Draw a 10 ml liquid dose from a vented vial and return the syringe to its rack.
comparisons.physical_skill: Insert a needle through a stopper, stabilize the barrel, pull the plunger accurately, withdraw, and reseat.
comparisons.success_condition: 9–11 ml liquid with at most 1 ml air, needle removed, syringe racked within pose tolerances, released, and arms returned.
comparisons.reason: It shares precision insertion and bimanual stabilization but tests dosing via coupled linear motions, not rotational locking and dynamic component tuning.

comparisons.objective: Uncap and spike an IV bag, then prime its drip chamber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a sliding bag, pull a breakaway cap, align and force-insert a spike, then squeeze-release the chamber.
comparisons.success_condition: Spike locked fully, chamber one-third to two-thirds full, bag remains on tray, hands release, and arms return.
comparisons.reason: Forceful insertion and priming are different tested abilities from fine hex engagement, collar adjustment, relocking, and repeated impact evaluation.

comparisons.objective: Remove spacer dowels so laminate settles and bonds accurately to a drawer front.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequentially pull full-length supports while controlling sag, tip, drag, and irreversible first contact.
comparisons.success_condition: All three laminate panels bond while registered within 6 mm in x and 8 mm in y, retaining edge overhang, with grippers clear for one second.
comparisons.reason: This tests controlled support removal and irreversible planar bonding, not adjustable mechanism locking or response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Load a plate on each dumbbell end and secure both with collars.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align plate and collar bores to sleeves, slide parts axially, release near obstructions, and push collars home.
comparisons.success_condition: Both plates are within 1 cm of their flanges and each has a locked collar no more than 6 mm away; unsecured plates fail.
comparisons.reason: It shares axial alignment and securing, but tests multi-part loading and safety retention rather than fine tool-mediated adjustment and iterative damping response.

comparisons.objective: Rearrange rack contents so frequently used items occupy the accessible middle shelf.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pick, transport, and stably place three household objects on different shelf levels.
comparisons.success_condition: Mug and tea tin are on the middle shelf; rarely used cake tin is on the top or bottom shelf, within pose and stillness tolerances.
comparisons.reason: Semantic storage planning and object relocation do not test mechanical unlocking, adjustment, relocking, or dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Open a cabinet, retrieve a multimeter, place it on the bench, and latch the door shut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Follow a hinged handle arc against a catch, hold the door while extracting a tool, place it, and reclose the catch.
comparisons.success_condition: Handle-mediated opening, multimeter removal and bench placement, caught door, stable cabinet, released objects, and arms returned.
comparisons.reason: Sequential articulated access and retrieval differ from fine fastener manipulation and tuning a damper through measured impact cycles.

comparisons.objective: Extract a stuck pin with a slide hammer and return the tool; candidate commissions an adjustable shock absorber through iterative impact testing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated bimanual momentum blows while stabilizing an aligned shaft, versus fine hex-bit seating, captive-screw torque, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin must come out through above-threshold impacts and the hammer be racked; candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J carriage stops within travel, rebound, force, lock-drift, and safety limits.
comparisons.reason: Both involve axial impact mechanics, but one tests generating extraction impulses with a slide hammer while the candidate tests tuning and locking a passive damper from measured response.

comparisons.objective: Place and release a drill guide in a structurally permitted joist zone; candidate commissions a robot-axis damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Rule-based spatial selection and stable placement, versus precision tool insertion, screw torque, collar adjustment, reacquisition, and test-fixture operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Guide must stand released on the centre line in the sole permitted zone; candidate requires safely locked adjustment and two compliant dynamic stops. The record gives no placement tolerance beyond its listed forbidden offsets, but the objectives are clearly unrelated.
comparisons.reason: The drill-guide task tests interpreting placement constraints, not mechanical adjustment or dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Glue a broken mug handle back in place; candidate commissions and locks an adjustable shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a rolling mug, apply adhesive to two patches, align two broken ends, and hold during cure, versus fine tool use, bounded torque, collar rotation, and iterative physical testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Both patches must receive glue and the handle must remain aligned for 3 seconds before release; candidate requires two safe repeatable impact cycles within quantified energy, travel, force, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Shared alignment and holding primitives do not equate adhesive repair with calibrated damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Refit and secure a bicycle quick-release wheel; candidate tunes and locks a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seat both axle ends in fork dropouts and close an over-centre lever in the safe orientation, versus hex-socket manipulation, fine collar rotation, and response-guided retuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Wheel must be fully seated before the lever is closed parallel/rearward along the fork; candidate requires a captive setscrew relocked and two compliant dynamic stops without overload or drift.
comparisons.reason: Both secure an adjustable mechanism, but they test materially different abilities: wheel/dropout assembly and over-centre closure versus instrumented damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Set a folding reading stand in its steepest ratchet notch; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Raise a hinged board past the top notch, lower the stay into it, release, and clear; candidate uses a fine hex tool and collar followed by iterative guarded impact tests.
comparisons.success_condition: Stay foot must occupy the top notch with the board within 5 degrees, still and hands clear; candidate requires two repeatable force- and travel-bounded stops with lock retention.
comparisons.reason: The record tests articulated ratchet engagement at a target angle, not precision screw locking or dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Hand-pollinate two female cucumber flowers in the correct transfer sequence; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate a light brush tip through millimetre-scale strokes, first on anthers then stigmas, versus hex-bit insertion, torque, collar rotation, and guarded testing.
comparisons.success_condition: A pollen-loaded brush must make ≥5 mm strokes within the stated 4 mm/1 mm contact region on both females; candidate requires two safe compliant impact cycles and no setting drift.
comparisons.reason: Although both demand fine tool-tip control and sequencing, pollen transfer and damper calibration test different physical outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Remove a locked head restraint and place it in a box; candidate adjusts and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: One arm holds a spring-loaded release while the other pulls two poles from guides, versus small-socket torque, tool withdrawal, collar rotation, and socket reacquisition.
comparisons.success_condition: Restraint must be raised, released without breaking the 15 N lock, removed, and boxed; candidate must satisfy quantified dynamic stopping limits over two cycles.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous release-and-extraction is materially different from fine adjustment followed by empirical dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Aim an inspection camera at a target without shifting its registered pivot; candidate commissions a shock absorber.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate two passive mount controls while preserving a datum, versus loosen-adjust-reacquire-tighten manipulation and iterative impact-response evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Camera axis must intersect the target, remain settled, retain the pivot, and finish hands-clear; the record omits numeric axis/pivot tolerances, while the candidate specifies energy, force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Despite both being adjustment tasks, aiming a registered optical axis tests coupled pointing and datum retention, not damping calibration or fine fastener handling.

comparisons.objective: Apply a complete opaque primer coat without drips; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load, rim-wipe, and stroke a flexible brush while managing finite paint volume, versus precision hex/collar manipulation and iterative guarded impact tests.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% of patches must be opaque with at most one drop, no bench brushing, and the brush released for full score; candidate requires two safe repeatable stops within mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: Material deposition and spill control are meaningfully different from adjustment locking and dynamic-response tuning.

comparisons.objective: Connect booster cables in a safe jump-start order; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open sprung clamps, align them around tapered posts/stud, release them to bite, and manage deformable leads, versus fine socket torque and collar adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Four spring-held connections must be made in the prescribed polarity/order with no forbidden contact; candidate requires lockout-safe adjustment and two compliant carriage cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both require safety sequencing, but electrical clamp placement and polarity management do not test damping adjustment or response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Fill and set down a cup at a sprung soda lever; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a cup aligned under a nozzle while sustaining lever force and stop at a visually controlled fill level, versus fine tool/collar handling and iterative impact evaluation.
comparisons.success_condition: Liquid must finish 0.5–2 cm below the rim with no overflow, spill, or >30-degree tip and the cup upright; candidate requires two bounded dynamic stops and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Sustained contact and fill-level control are different tested abilities from mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Remove a recessed book from a packed shelf without disturbing neighbours; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tip the book by its exposed head, acquire a new grasp, transfer it, and release it safely, versus socket insertion, screw torque, collar rotation, and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Book must rest released on the mat while neighbours remain within tilt/displacement limits and book speed stays below 0.6 m/s; candidate uses force, energy, travel, rebound, and drift criteria.
comparisons.reason: The record tests access creation and regrasp in clutter, not adjustment and dynamic calibration.

comparisons.objective: Remove one bottle from a crowded row and place it in a tray; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clearance-sensitive grasp and transport without toppling adjacent fragile objects, versus fine fastener/collar manipulation and test-fixture operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Red bottle must be upright in the tray without another bottle exceeding the tilt/displacement limits; candidate requires two safe repeatable impact stops.
comparisons.reason: Crowded-object extraction is unrelated to tuning and locking a passive shock absorber.

comparisons.objective: Open a drawer after removing the bar that restrains it; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Diagnose obstruction, slide a long bar axially from two sleeves, then pull a drawer, versus loosen-adjust-relock fine manipulation and iterative dynamic tests.
comparisons.success_condition: Bar must clear both sleeves and the drawer open at least 18 cm without damage or cabinet motion; candidate requires bounded forces, 12 mm travel, safe sequencing, and two stable cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both involve releasing a restraint before motion, but the drawer task tests obstruction removal rather than precision locking and response calibration.

comparisons.objective: Open a sliding door after clearing a block from its track; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Identify and lift an obstruction, then hand off long-range sliding between arms without derailment, versus fine hex/collar manipulation and test cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Door must reach within 2 cm of the end stop, remain in its track, and leave the block safely on the table; candidate requires two non-bottoming force-bounded stops.
comparisons.reason: Obstacle diagnosis and long-travel door handling are materially different from damper adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Hook a wire to fish tape and pull it through a bent conduit; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Make a small hook-eye connection, manage two deformable chains, and pull hand-over-hand through a bore, versus rigid fine-tool insertion, torque, collar rotation, and testing.
comparisons.success_condition: The hooked wire end must emerge at least 5 cm from the far mouth without premature tape removal or hand-feeding; candidate requires two repeatable compliant stops within mechanical limits.
comparisons.reason: Shared small-feature alignment is generic; maintaining a deformable pulling joint through conduit tests a different ability.

comparisons.objective: Insert a USB-C plug into a handheld spot welder and set the assembly down; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually orient a handheld device and align a rigid plug within submillimetre port clearance, versus insert/withdraw a hex bit, apply bounded torque, rotate a collar, and reacquire a moving socket.
comparisons.success_condition: Plug must meet 0.5 mm centre, 1.5 mm depth, and 8-degree angular conditions and remain inserted after release; candidate additionally tests locking and iterative dynamic performance.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest shared insertion primitive, but USB connector mating does not test adjustable-mechanism unlocking, setting, relocking, or response-based commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Install an 18650 cell with correct polarity and latch the welder lid; candidate commissions a damper.

comparisons.success_condition: Cell must be seated positive-end-first within 3 mm/10 degrees, lid latched within 2 degrees, and welder safely released; candidate requires two quantified safe stopping cycles.

comparisons.objective: Return two stranded slot cars to active lanes without interrupting a circulating protected car; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Assigned-arm pickup, guide-slot insertion, timed release into moving traffic, and collision avoidance, versus fine fastener/collar work and guarded impact testing.
comparisons.success_condition: Each car must independently travel 100 mm clockwise while lane-engaged after release; any protected-car contact zeros the score. Numeric insertion tolerances are absent, but the outcome is clearly different.

comparisons.objective: Connect a flexible sensor cable to a ZIF connector; candidate commissions and locks a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open a tiny latch, grasp a flex cable mid-length, slide it fully into a zero-force slot, hold it seated, and close the latch bimanually; candidate seats a hex bit, loosens a captive screw, rotates a collar, reacquires the socket, and tightens.
comparisons.success_condition: Latch must be opened before insertion and closed while the cable remains seated; the record gives no numeric seating/latch tolerances. Candidate further requires quantified dynamic validation over two cycles.
comparisons.reason: Both feature ordered unlock-manipulate-relock actions, but ZIF flex insertion tests compliant-part handling and latch coordination, whereas the candidate tests rotary adjustment plus empirical damper commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Crack an egg into a bowl and dispose of both shell halves; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually tap a fragile shell, pull halves apart, manage released contents, and sort shells, versus precision tool torque and collar tuning.
comparisons.success_condition: Yolk and at least five white drops must reach the bowl, both shells the tray, with no shell in the bowl; candidate requires two safe, repeatable impact stops.
comparisons.reason: Fragile-object fracture and contents control are materially unrelated to mechanical adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Return a beehive frame onto both rests and close the gap to neighbouring frames; candidate commissions a damper.

comparisons.success_condition: Both lugs must support a level, square frame with ≤2 mm neighbour gap and no other frame displaced; candidate requires locked setting and two force/travel-bounded cycles.
comparisons.reason: Large-part insertion and lateral seating test a different ability from shock-absorber tuning.

comparisons.objective: Fasten an instrument case using separate spring hooks and safety catches; candidate commissions a damper.
comparisons.physical_skill: Choose keepers, engage and tension two loose spring hooks, then set independent catches while protecting case contents, versus captive-screw/collar manipulation and guarded cycling.
comparisons.success_condition: Closed case must remain fastened hands-off for 20 seconds while cases and instruments stay upright. The record omits exact hook/catch tolerances and force thresholds; candidate instead uses explicit dynamic force, travel, rebound, and drift limits.
comparisons.reason: Although both require secure locking, multi-hook case closure and retention do not test adjustable damping or iterative calibration.

comparisons.objective: Trace hidden crossed cables and place the two correct plugs in matching holders; candidate commissions a damper.

comparisons.success_condition: Both correct plugs must be released in their holders while three distractor plugs remain within 5 cm and no cable pulls out; candidate requires two safe repeatable stops and retained setting.
comparisons.reason: Hidden-endpoint identification and deformable manipulation are different from mechanical commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Place and snap-latch a case lid while bracing an unstable case; candidate commissions and locks a damper.

comparisons.success_condition: Both latches must click with lid centre within 3 mm and angle within 5 degrees, case motion constrained, and hands clear; candidate additionally requires two quantified physical stopping cycles.
comparisons.reason: Shared alignment and locking are generic; snap-fit assembly under bracing tests a different mechanism and outcome from iterative damping adjustment.

comparisons.objective: Plug a cord, route it through a floor-box notch, and close the cover without pinching it.

comparisons.reason: The candidate tunes and locks a captive-set-screw damper, then validates dynamic stopping. This record tests cable routing, plug insertion, and lid placement, with no adjustment locking or impact-response commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Partition five weighted parcels between two totes without exceeding either weight limit.

comparisons.objective: Sort only cast ballots into color-matched trays while excluding an uncast ballot.

comparisons.objective: Align a torqued castle nut's slot by further tightening and insert a cotter pin.

comparisons.objective: Index a wafer while preventing probes from scratching it.

comparisons.objective: Register a windowed plate behind an inspection screen despite grasp-induced visual occlusion.

comparisons.objective: Remove an optical instrument from fitted foam, place it on a stand, and collect the inserts safely.

comparisons.success_condition: Instrument and inserts placed without drop, excessive tilt, or unsupported descent; the body reports measured controls but not the complete numeric rubric.

comparisons.objective: Close only cabinet doors that begin open without toggling already-latched doors.

comparisons.objective: Feed a cable plug through a panel grommet, hand it over, and pull the cable to a marked depth.

comparisons.objective: Support a precision bar with one arm before withdrawing its carriage with the other.

comparisons.reason: This is support handoff and extraction sequencing, not fastener/collar manipulation or iterative dynamic commissioning.

comparisons.objective: Raise and rotate a monitor while managing independent spring index locks, then relock it.

comparisons.success_condition: Screen raised 130 mm and pivoted 90 degrees with tilt preserved, locks engaged, force/contact limits respected, and hands off for 20 seconds.

The candidate uniquely combines recessed hex access, captive-screw loosening, fine collar tuning, socket reacquisition, and repeated impact-response criteria; its success is not merely a locked pose.

comparisons.objective: Close the unsafe wide dispenser opening, invert the bottle, open the perforated side, and season food within a dose limit.

comparisons.objective: Install a long blind headrail into two brackets and close both retaining gates.

comparisons.success_condition: Rail depth, floor contact, tilt, gate angles, and release determine success; no dynamic stopping response or force/energy limits are tested.

comparisons.objective: Remove a towel obstructing a rice-cooker vent, then press the COOK control safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Moves a loose obstruction and depresses a spring-return button; it lacks tool insertion, torque, collar rotation, socket reacquisition, and response-based adjustment.
comparisons.success_condition: Vent clearance before activation, released control, supported towel, and stable finish are required; damper travel, rebound, forces, and repeated impact cycles are absent.
comparisons.reason: The shared actuation of a physical control is generic. The central tested ability is hazard removal before appliance activation. No separate spec supplies tighter thresholds, but the objective is clearly unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Press a loose AED pad flat, clear both hands from the patient, and press SHOCK.

comparisons.objective: Correct a randomized liquid dose to 10.000 ± 0.050 g using balance feedback, then discard the pipette.

comparisons.success_condition: Final liquid mass, beaker stability, and pipette disposal determine success; the damper's travel, force, rebound, and lock-drift limits are absent.
comparisons.reason: Although both iterate from measured feedback, one tests precision liquid metering and the other mechanical energy absorption plus locking. The record does not provide a full scoring spec beyond the body, but the outcome differs decisively.

comparisons.objective: Dispense coffee using a spring-return shelf and return a filled mug safely to its saucer.

comparisons.success_condition: Retained volume, zero spill, vessel choice, wall/stream safety, and final placement are scored; no repeated carriage-stop performance is required.

comparisons.objective: Remove diagonal cutters from an upturned peg in clutter and place them on a mat without dislodging neighbors.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasps, lifts, pulls, and places a hanging tool amid obstacles; no bit insertion, captive screw manipulation, or tuning loop.
comparisons.success_condition: Cutter position, stillness, neighbor retention, and fall avoidance determine score; mechanical setting retention and dynamic stopping are not involved.
comparisons.reason: This tests constrained tool retrieval, not using a fine tool to unlock, adjust, relock, and validate a component.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a flashlight tail cap, set it down, tip out the battery, and return the flashlight.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually stabilizes a threaded object, performs multiple regrasped twists with axial rise, and pours out a cell.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap separation and safe placement, battery collection, and flashlight return are scored; there is no captive screw, preserved setting, or dynamic calibration.

comparisons.objective: Arrange five glazed pots upright in a kiln with clearance from pots, posts, and walls.

comparisons.success_condition: Each pot must meet 2 cm inter-object/post and 1.5 cm wall clearances, with any contact invalidating the load.
comparisons.reason: This tests collision-free batch layout and placement, not commissioning a dynamic component. The body omits detailed pose tolerances beyond clearances, but the objective remains clearly different.

comparisons.objective: Sort rigid cloth surrogates into buckets according to a hygiene color code.
comparisons.physical_skill: Performs labeled pick-and-place sorting; no alignment into a fine socket, rotary locking, or physical response measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Final bucket membership determines score, including a penalty for cross-contamination; no mechanical damage or cycle-performance criteria apply.
comparisons.reason: The task is semantic sorting with simple transport, meaningfully different from dexterous damper adjustment and test.

comparisons.objective: Place decking bundles across at least three joists near a bearing end, including a handoff.

comparisons.success_condition: Joist coverage, bearing-end distance, flatness, and non-stacking are required; dynamic stopping and setting retention are absent.

comparisons.objective: Seat a screwdriver in a fitted foam cutout, close the case, and press until its clasp catches.

comparisons.reason: Both require a physical lock and final tool clearance, but this task tests storage fit and snap closure, not preservation and validation of a tuned mechanical setting.

comparisons.objective: Select photo-matching parts from a moving conveyor and assemble a model while staging early arrivals and avoiding a jam.

comparisons.reason: This tests visual selection and temporal assembly planning on a conveyor, not damper commissioning. Detailed final pose thresholds are absent from the record body, but no plausible duplicate ability is indicated.

comparisons.objective: Eject a used pipette tip hands-free, press-fit a fresh tip, and return the pipette to its stand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Aligns a held pipette with a fixed ejector fork and tip rack, applies seating force, and transports a friction-retained tip.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct disposal, fresh-tip retention, redocking, and avoidance of hand contact, drops, or tip-over are required.
